items.name: Numerical Picard local system
items.statement: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k (not necessarily reduced, irreducible or equidimensional). Pic^τ_{X/k} ⊂ Pic_{X/k} is the open and closed subgroup scheme of finite type parametrizing invertible sheaves that are numerically trivial on the geometric fibre. Num_{X/k} = Pic_{X/k}/Pic^τ_{X/k} is an étale group scheme, the local system of numerical classes. It corresponds to the Galois module Num_{X/k}(k^sep) = Num_{X/k}(k^alg) ≅ Z^{⊕ρ}, where ρ ≥ 0 is the Picard number of X_{k^alg}. Num_{X/k} is constant if Gal(k^sep/k) acts trivially, equivalently Num_{X/k} ≅ (Z^{⊕ρ})_k.

tests.name: NumericalPicardlocalsystemTest1
tests.statement: Num(P¹_k)=Z via degree.

tests.name: NumericalPicardlocalsystemTest2
tests.statement: Numerically trivial bundles map to zero, including torsion bundles.

tests.name: NumericalPicardlocalsystemTest3
tests.statement: For P¹_C viewed over R, geometric Num is Z² with nontrivial conjugation; it is not constant.

items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the definition of 'constant' (trivial Galois action on Num_{X/k}(k^sep) ≅ Z^ρ), which every later item uses, and that Pic^τ is of finite type (needed for Num to be étale with finitely generated stalk). §1 also allows X non-reduced, reducible or non-equidimensional. Review note: missing is right. Neither library has Picard schemes of proper schemes over a field. The existence and finiteness input is proposed below as a new item (SGA 6 XIII 4.7). /211 gives only algebraic-space representability in flat families.

items.name: Positive-power descent criterion
items.statement: For proper X/k, Num_{X/k} is constant iff some positive integer d has this property: for every line bundle L on X_kalg there exists a numerically trivial line bundle N on X_kalg such that L^⊗d⊗N descends to X.
items.note: Use d≥1; printed d≥0 admits the vacuous value zero. Arbitrary proper X, not only geometrically connected X. Review note: missing is right. E1 is confirmed, so d ≥ 1 is correct. The proof needs /8, /208 and three results no item states: the Picard scheme and its τ-part over a field, the torsion of Pic^τ-torsor classes, and the Leray sequence Pic(X) → Pic_{X/k}(k) → H²(k, h_*G_m). All three are proposed under coverage. The printed proof also has a harmless error, recorded as a new issue: P′ should be Pic^τ_{X′/E}, and R¹pr_*P′ = 0 is false in general but not used.

items.name: Component dual graph
items.statement: For a noetherian scheme Z, the dual graph Γ(Z) has the irreducible components Z_i as vertices, with an edge between distinct Z_i and Z_j if and only if Z_i ∩ Z_j ≠ ∅. A morphism Z′ → Z that maps each irreducible component of Z′ into an irreducible component of Z (for example a flat morphism) induces a map on vertices. Under this map, adjacent vertices go to adjacent or equal vertices. It is a graph isomorphism if it is bijective on vertices and on edges. When it is bijective on vertices, it sends edges to edges.

tests.name: ComponentdualgraphTest1
tests.statement: An integral curve has one vertex.

tests.name: ComponentdualgraphTest2
tests.statement: Two components meeting at two points still give one adjacency edge in this convention.

tests.name: ComponentdualgraphTest3
tests.statement: A disconnected union of two curves has no edge.

items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the induced graph morphism and the notion of graph isomorphism that Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 2.1 use. The paper's claim that a component-preserving morphism 'sends edges to edges' is false; see the new issue. The corrected statement records the true behaviour.

items.name: Curve criterion for numerical constancy
items.statement: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k all of whose irreducible components are one-dimensional. Then Num_{X/k} is constant if and only if Γ(X_{k^alg}) → Γ(X) is a graph isomorphism.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: False as stated when X has zero-dimensional irreducible components. §1 explicitly allows non-equidimensional X. For k = ℝ and X = P¹_ℝ ⊔ Spec ℂ, Num_{X/ℝ} = Z is constant, but Γ(X_ℂ) has 3 vertices and Γ(X) has 2. The proof uses a degree and an effective Cartier divisor on every component. Recorded as a new issue. Review note: missing is right. The paper never uses Proposition 1.2 again (the TeX has no other \ref to it).

items.name: Contraction
items.statement: A contraction of proper schemes is a proper morphism f:X→Y for which O_Y→f_*O_X is an isomorphism.

tests.name: ContractionTest1
tests.statement: The identity is a contraction.

tests.name: ContractionTest2
tests.statement: A connected-fiber morphism with Stein factor O_Y is a contraction.

tests.name: ContractionTest3
tests.statement: A disconnected finite étale cover of degree two is not a contraction.

items.name: Descent of geometric contractions
items.statement: Let X/k be proper with constant Num_{X/k}. Every contraction X_{kalg}→Y with projective target descends to a contraction X→Y₀ over k.
items.note: The target's projectivity is a hypothesis; descent includes its identification after base change. Review note: missing is right. The proof needs /5, /7, /8 and three results proposed under coverage: semiample contractions (including that numerically equivalent semiample sheaves define the same contraction), spreading out a contraction to a finite extension (EGA IV 8.8.2), and the Brauer obstruction sequence. The splitting of a normal extension into Galois and purely inseparable parts is in Mathlib (separableClosure.isGalois, separableClosure.isPurelyInseparable).

items.name: Purely inseparable contraction descent
items.statement: For a purely inseparable field extension k⊂k′, every contraction of X_{k′}, with X proper over k, descends to k; this branch does not require constant Num or projectivity of the target.
items.locator: proof of Theorem 1.3 and the remark after it, p. 7
items.note: Review note: missing is right. The proof also needs descent of finite type, separatedness and properness along field extensions, flat base change of global sections, and that purely inseparable base change is a universal homeomorphism. These are proposed under coverage. E2 (U′ = f′⁻¹(V′)) is confirmed.

items.name: Torsion in the Picard descent obstruction
items.statement: Let h: X → S = Spec k be proper and X^aff = Spec H⁰(X, O_X), a finite k-algebra. Then H²(S, h_*G_{m,X}) ≅ Br(X^aff) = H²(X^aff, G_m), and this group is torsion.
items.note: Proof reduces via the finite Artin affinization algebra, its nilpotent filtration, and field Brauer groups. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the identification that Lemma 1.4 states: H²(Spec k, h_*G_m) ≅ Br(X^aff) with X^aff = Spec H⁰(X, O_X). Wrong page. Review note: missing is right. The R¹ step is in Mathlib: the instance that the Picard group of a semilocal ring is trivial (Mathlib/RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean:545, [Finite (MaximalSpectrum R)] : Subsingleton (Pic R)), read at 082e2d3. The cohomological Brauer group of a finite k-algebra and its torsion are in neither library; proposed under coverage.

items.name: Intersection-labelled component graph
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k with h⁰(O_S) = 1, and C ⊂ S a curve with irreducible components C_1, …, C_r and multiplicities m_i ≥ 1. Its intersection matrix is N(C) = (C_i·C_j)_{1≤i,j≤r} ∈ Mat_r(Z). C is negative-definite (resp. negative-semidefinite) if N(C) is. The dual graph Γ(C) becomes an edge-labelled graph by giving the edge between C_i ≠ C_j the label (C_i·C_j) > 0, the intersection number on S.

tests.name: IntersectionlabelledcomponentgraphTest1
tests.statement: Transverse rational components meeting once have label 1.

tests.name: IntersectionlabelledcomponentgraphTest2
tests.statement: Two components meeting transversely twice have label 2.

tests.name: IntersectionlabelledcomponentgraphTest3
tests.statement: The unlabelled graph alone cannot distinguish labels 1 and 2.

items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the intersection matrix N(C) and the notions of negative-definite and negative-semidefinite curves, defined in the same paragraph and used in the proof of Theorem 2.1. The item should also say that labels are intersection numbers on S over k. For fibres over non-rational points this normalization matters; see /11.

items.name: Fiber graph descent
items.statement: Let f:S→Z be a contraction of a smooth proper k-surface with H⁰(O_S)=k. Let ā:Spec Ω→Z have image a, with Ω algebraically closed, and suppose S_ā is one-dimensional. If Num_{S/k} is constant, Γ(S_ā)→Γ(S_a) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Review note: missing is right. The proof needs four results proposed under coverage: the contraction trichotomy, negativity of exceptional curves, Zariski's lemma, and Zariski connectedness. The fibre-type step has a small gap, recorded as a new issue with its one-line fix. E3 (X for S) is confirmed.

items.name: Descent of fiber intersection labels
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k with h⁰(O_S) = 1 and Num_{S/k} constant. Let f: S → Z be a contraction and ā: Spec Ω → Z a geometric point with image a and S_ā one-dimensional. Suppose (S_a)_red is geometrically reduced over κ(a). If S_ā is reducible, then κ(a) = k. Moreover, the graph isomorphism Γ(S_ā) → Γ(S_a) of Theorem 2.1(i) respects edge labels: for components C_i, C_j of S_ā lying over components D_i, D_j of S_a, (C_i·C_j) on S_Ω equals (D_i·D_j) on S.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: 'Geometrically reduced' must be over κ(a). With /9's labels (intersection numbers on S over k), a pair of components D_i, D_j of S_a satisfies (D_i·D_j) = [κ(a):k]·(C_i·C_j). Label preservation therefore needs κ(a) = k whenever S_ā is reducible. The paper's 'immediate from (i)' proof does not supply this; recorded as a gap with the fix. The statement itself is true.

items.name: Residue field of a reducible geometric fiber
items.statement: Under Theorem 2.1, if S_ā is reducible, the field extension k⊂κ(a) is purely inseparable.
items.note: Review note: missing is right. The paper's statement is right but not sharp: for smooth S, the argument in the Theorem 2.1(ii) gap below shows κ(a) = k.

items.name: Curves of fiber and canonical type
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k with h⁰(O_S) = 1, and C = Σ_{i=0}^r m_iC_i a curve with irreducible components C_i and multiplicities m_i ≥ 1. C is of fibre type if (C·C_i) = 0 for all i; the condition passes to multiples and connected components. A connected curve of fibre type with gcd(m_0, …, m_r) = 1 is an indecomposable curve of fibre type. C is of canonical type if (C·C_i) = (K_S·C_i) = 0 for all i.

tests.name: CurvesoffiberandcanonicaltypeTest1
tests.statement: A smooth genus-one fiber has multiplicity 1.

tests.name: CurvesoffiberandcanonicaltypeTest2
tests.statement: Twice an indecomposable fiber has multiplicity 2 and the same underlying divisor.

tests.name: CurvesoffiberandcanonicaltypeTest3
tests.statement: A negative-definite exceptional divisor is not of fiber type.

items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: The paper's 'fibre type' does not require connectedness; the condition passes to multiples and connected components. 'Canonical type' means (C·C_i) = (K_S·C_i) = 0 for all i, with no indecomposability; the item's 'if also' can be read as requiring it. Wrong locator: these definitions are on p. 9. The Zariski-lemma assertion of the same paragraph is proposed as a separate new item.

items.name: Rationality of singular-fiber components over finite fields
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k = F_q with h⁰(O_S) = 1 and Num_{S/k} constant. Let f: S → B be a relatively minimal genus-one fibration, and ā a geometric point over a closed point a ∈ B. Then Γ(S_ā) → Γ(S_a) is a graph isomorphism respecting edge labels. If S_ā is reducible, a is F_q-rational. If every irreducible component of S_a is birational to P¹_{F_q}, a is rational. If a is rational and f⁻¹_ind(ā) is singular, every irreducible component of S_a is birational to P¹_{F_q}, and its normalization is isomorphic to P¹_{F_q}.
items.note: Added singularity restriction: the displayed equivalence in the preprint is false for a smooth elliptic fiber. The graph-descent assertion itself has no such restriction. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Missing 'relatively minimal', a standing assumption of §3 (p. 9). Without it (ii)⇒(iii) fails even for singular fibres. Take S = Bl_P(E × P¹_{F_q}) with P an F_q-point: Num is constant, and the fibre through P is Ẽ + L, reducible over a rational point, with the elliptic component Ẽ. The item also drops Proposition 3.1's first assertion (graph isomorphism respecting edge labels). E4 is confirmed.

items.name: Split semistable fiber count
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over F_q with h⁰(O_S) = 1 and Num_{S/F_q} constant, f: S → B a relatively minimal genus-one fibration, and C = f⁻¹(a) the schematic fibre over an F_q-rational point a ∈ B, with r ≥ 1 irreducible components and C_red singular. If C_ind has the split Kodaira symbol I_r, then Card C(F_q) = rq.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Missing 'relatively minimal' (the Kodaira symbols presuppose it) and h⁰(O_S) = 1. The count is of the schematic fibre C = f⁻¹(a); multiplicities do not change it.

items.name: Nonsplit nodal fiber count
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over F_q with h⁰(O_S) = 1 and Num_{S/F_q} constant, f: S → B a relatively minimal genus-one fibration, and C = f⁻¹(a) the schematic fibre over an F_q-rational point a ∈ B, with r ≥ 1 irreducible components and C_red singular. If C_ind has the twisted symbol Ĩ₁ (non-split I₁, so r = 1), then Card C(F_q) = q + 2.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Missing 'relatively minimal' (the Kodaira symbols presuppose it) and h⁰(O_S) = 1. The count is of the schematic fibre C = f⁻¹(a); multiplicities do not change it.

items.name: Nonsplit two-component fiber count
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over F_q with h⁰(O_S) = 1 and Num_{S/F_q} constant, f: S → B a relatively minimal genus-one fibration, and C = f⁻¹(a) the schematic fibre over an F_q-rational point a ∈ B, with r ≥ 1 irreducible components and C_red singular. items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Missing 'relatively minimal' (the Kodaira symbols presuppose it) and h⁰(O_S) = 1. The count is of the schematic fibre C = f⁻¹(a); multiplicities do not change it.

items.name: Additive fiber count
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over F_q with h⁰(O_S) = 1 and Num_{S/F_q} constant, f: S → B a relatively minimal genus-one fibration, and C = f⁻¹(a) the schematic fibre over an F_q-rational point a ∈ B, with r ≥ 1 irreducible components and C_red singular. If C_ind has an unstable (additive) Kodaira symbol, then Card C(F_q) = rq + 1.

items.name: No I₀* fiber over F₂ with constant numerical Picard
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over F₂ with h⁰(O_S) = 1 and Num_{S/F₂} constant, and f: S → B a relatively minimal genus-one fibration. Then no geometric fibre of f has Kodaira symbol I₀*. A reducible geometric fibre lies over an F₂-rational point (/12). There all five components are isomorphic to P¹_{F₂} (/14), and the four terminal components would meet the central one in four distinct rational points, but Card P¹(F₂) = 3.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Not self-contained ('Such a fibration'). It should exclude I₀* at every closed point, as the paper does, not only at rational points.

items.name: Elliptic curve E1 over F₂
items.statement: The smooth projective Weierstrass curve y²+y=x³+x²+1 over F₂ has cyclic rational-point group of order 1, j=0, and is supersingular.
acceptance: Explicitly enumerate the F₂ affine points and include the point at infinity.
items.note: Review note: Checked by computation: Δ = 1, so the curve is smooth. c₄ ≡ 0 mod 2, so j = 0. The F₂-points are ∞ only. missing is right as a statement. Its ingredients are in the libraries: mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.j (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Weierstrass.lean:389), mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.j_eq_zero_iff_of_char_two (:420), and tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.pointCount (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/PointCount.lean:69). items.name: Five elliptic isomorphism classes over F₂
items.statement: Every elliptic curve over F₂ is isomorphic over F₂ to exactly one of E₁,…,E₅ of Proposition 3.3; its number of F₂-points determines the class.
items.note: Finite Weierstrass-coordinate enumeration independently checked; this does not classify genus-one fibrations. Review note: missing is right. There are five classes (three with j = 0, two with j = 1), distinguished by their point counts. The coordinate changes are mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.VariableChange (/200).

items.name: Enriques surface
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k, an Enriques surface is a smooth proper k-surface Y with H⁰(O_Y)=k, numerically trivial canonical class, and ℓ-adic b₂=10 (ℓ≠char k). Over other fields use this geometric condition.

tests.name: EnriquessurfaceTest1
tests.statement: A characteristic-two classical Enriques surface has nontrivial canonical bundle of order 2.

tests.name: EnriquessurfaceTest2
tests.statement: The numerical condition is weaker than requiring the canonical bundle to be trivial.

tests.name: EnriquessurfaceTest3
tests.statement: A K3 surface, with b₂=22, is not Enriques.

items.name: Numerically trivial Picard group of an Enriques surface
items.statement: For an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field, Pic^τ is finite of length 2 and its k-points are generated by ω_Y.

items.name: Enriques numerical and cohomological invariants
items.statement: For such Y, Num(Y) is free of rank 10, b₁=b₃=0, b₂=ρ=10, and h¹(O_Y)=h²(O_Y)≤1.

items.name: Enriques numerical lattice
items.statement: The intersection form on Num(Y) is even unimodular of signature(1,9), and Num(Y)≅U⊕E₈(-1), where U has Gram matrix [[0,1],[1,0]].
items.note: The geometric identification is missing; the abstract E₈ and integral-lattice APIs are already built and imported.

items.name: Existence of genus-one fibrations
items.statement: Every Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field admits a genus-one fibration to P¹.

items.name: Double fibers
items.statement: Every genus-one fibration on such an Enriques surface has a multiple fiber, and every multiple fiber has multiplicity 2.

items.name: Integral two-sections
items.statement: Every genus-one fibration on such a surface has an integral two-section, which can be chosen as either a (-2)-curve or a half-fiber of another genus-one fibration.
items.note: Never replace an integral two-section by a (-2)-curve without proof.

items.name: Half-fiber
items.statement: A half-fiber F of a genus-one fibration on an Enriques surface is the effective divisor with 2F equal to a fiber over a rational base point.
api: fiber class equals twice half-fiber class
uniqueness from its effective line bundle

tests.name: HalffiberTest1
tests.statement: F²=0.

tests.name: HalffiberTest2
tests.statement: A two-section C has C·F=1.

tests.name: HalffiberTest3
tests.statement: The reduced support of a reducible double fiber need not equal its half-fiber divisor.

items.name: Classical Enriques criteria
items.statement: For an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field, these are equivalent: ω_Y has order 2; H¹(O_Y)=0; some genus-one fibration has no wild fibers; some genus-one fibration has two multiple fibers.

items.name: Tame double fibers and canonical bundle
items.statement: Under those equivalent conditions every genus-one fibration has exactly two tame double fibers 2F₁,2F₂, with ω_Y≅O_Y(F₁−F₂); the conditions always hold if char k≠2.

items.name: Characteristic-two tame half-fiber types
items.statement: If char k=2 and a genus-one fibration on an Enriques surface has two distinct double fibers 2F₁,2F₂, each F_i is ordinary elliptic or unstable; neither is supersingular elliptic or semistable.

items.name: ordinary Enriques surface
items.statement: In characteristic 2 an Enriques surface is ordinary iff Pic^τ=μ₂; its Cartier-dual canonical-cover group is Z/2, its étale fundamental group is Z/2, and its canonical bundle is trivial.
api: type under algebraically closed field extension

tests.name: ordinaryEnriquessurfaceTest1
tests.statement: The Picard group scheme for this type is μ₂.

tests.name: ordinaryEnriquessurfaceTest2
tests.statement: The cover group is the Cartier dual Z/2, not Pic^τ itself.

tests.name: ordinaryEnriquessurfaceTest3
tests.statement: The type is disjoint from the other two characteristic-two types.

items.name: classical Enriques surface
items.statement: In characteristic 2 an Enriques surface is classical iff Pic^τ=Z/2; its Cartier-dual canonical-cover group is μ₂, its étale fundamental group is trivial, and its canonical bundle is order 2.
api: type under algebraically closed field extension

tests.name: classicalEnriquessurfaceTest1
tests.statement: The Picard group scheme for this type is Z/2.

tests.name: classicalEnriquessurfaceTest2
tests.statement: The cover group is the Cartier dual μ₂, not Pic^τ itself.

tests.name: classicalEnriquessurfaceTest3
tests.statement: The type is disjoint from the other two characteristic-two types.

items.name: supersingular Enriques surface
items.statement: In characteristic 2 an Enriques surface is supersingular iff Pic^τ=α₂; its Cartier-dual canonical-cover group is α₂, its étale fundamental group is trivial, and its canonical bundle is trivial.
api: type under algebraically closed field extension

tests.name: supersingularEnriquessurfaceTest1
tests.statement: The Picard group scheme for this type is α₂.

tests.name: supersingularEnriquessurfaceTest2
tests.statement: The cover group is the Cartier dual α₂, not Pic^τ itself.

tests.name: supersingularEnriquessurfaceTest3
tests.statement: The type is disjoint from the other two characteristic-two types.

items.name: K3-like canonical covering
items.statement: For a simply connected Enriques surface in characteristic 2 (classical or supersingular), the inclusion Pic^τ→Pic determines a nontrivial torsor X→Y for its local Cartier dual; this universal homeomorphism is called its K3-like covering.

tests.name: KlikecanonicalcoveringTest1
tests.statement: The cover has degree 2.

tests.name: KlikecanonicalcoveringTest2
tests.statement: Its total space is integral and Cohen–Macaulay with ω_X trivial.

tests.name: KlikecanonicalcoveringTest3
tests.statement: The total space is singular, so K3-like does not mean a smooth K3 surface.

items.name: Cohomology of the K3-like cover
items.statement: For the preceding canonical cover, h⁰(O_X)=h²(O_X)=1 and h¹(O_X)=0, and its singular locus is nonempty.

items.name: Conductrix and exceptionality
items.statement: For a simply connected characteristic-two Enriques surface, let X′ be the normalization of its K3-like cover. The map X′→Y is finite flat purely inseparable of degree 2. The ramification divisor R′ for X′→X is pulled back from an effective Cartier divisor C on Y, the conductrix; 2C is the biconductrix. Y is exceptional iff h¹(O_{2C})≠0.

tests.name: ConductrixandexceptionalityTest1
tests.statement: If C=0 then h¹(O_{2C})=0.

tests.name: ConductrixandexceptionalityTest2
tests.statement: The biconductrix is twice C as a divisor.

tests.name: ConductrixandexceptionalityTest3
tests.statement: Simply connected alone does not imply exceptional.

items.name: Nonexceptional quasielliptic restriction
items.statement: On a nonexceptional Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, no quasielliptic fibration has a simple III* or II* fiber.

items.name: Nonexceptional multiple exceptional-type restriction
items.statement: On such a surface, no genus-one fibration with a multiple IV*, III*, or II* fiber admits a (-2)-curve two-section.

items.name: Partner genus-one fibration
items.statement: For every genus-one fibration on a nonexceptional Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, another genus-one fibration has fiber-class intersection 4 with it.

items.name: Family of Enriques surfaces
items.statement: Over a ring R, an Enriques family is a flat proper finitely presented algebraic space Y→Spec R whose geometric fibers are Enriques surfaces. Isomorphisms and base change give the fppf stack M_Enr over affine Z-schemes.

tests.name: FamilyofEnriquessurfacesTest1
tests.statement: A family pulls back to every R-algebra.

tests.name: FamilyofEnriquessurfacesTest2
tests.statement: Over an algebraically closed field this recovers the surface definition.

tests.name: FamilyofEnriquessurfacesTest3
tests.statement: Restricting the definition to schemes would lose the stated algebraic-space scope.

items.name: No Enriques surface over the integers
items.statement: There is no Enriques family over Z; equivalently M_Enr(Z) is empty.
items.note: Depends on the repaired Proposition 5.5 chain /63, Fontaine /147–/148, the exceptional lifting input /48, and the full finite-field endpoint /146. Recursive source closure remains partial.

items.name: Exceptional fibers do not lift modulo four
items.statement: There is no Enriques family over Z/4Z whose geometric special fiber is exceptional.

items.name: Relative Picard representability
items.statement: For an Enriques family over any ring R, its fppf relative Picard algebraic space is a scheme.

items.name: Relative numerical invariants
items.statement: For such a family, Pic^τ is an open subgroup locally free of rank 2 and Num is an étale local system of free abelian groups of rank 10.

items.name: Rank-two Oort–Tate group
items.statement: For an invertible R-module L and a∈L,b∈L^(-1) with a⊗b=2, define G(A)={f∈L⊗A:f²=a f}, with operation f⋆g=f+g−bfg.

tests.name: RanktwoOortTategroupTest1
tests.statement: (L,a,b)=(R,1, 2) gives the constant group Z/2.

tests.name: RanktwoOortTategroupTest2
tests.statement: (R,2, 1) gives μ₂ via u=1−f.

tests.name: RanktwoOortTategroupTest3
tests.statement: The plus sign fails over Z at a=1,b=2,f=g=1:4 is not idempotent.

items.name: Classification of finite flat groups of rank two
items.statement: Every finite locally free group scheme of rank 2 over a ring R is isomorphic to the group associated with an invertible module and a⊗b=2 as above.
items.note: Introduction and exact rank-two contract read; full classification proof not yet extracted.

items.name: Rank-two Cartier duality
items.statement: The Cartier dual of the group associated with (L,a,b) is associated with (L^(-1),b,a).

items.name: Rank-two groups over Z
items.statement: Over Z every finite flat rank-two group is isomorphic to Z/2 or μ₂.
items.locator: §5, p. 14 (Tate–Oort classification) and proof of Proposition 5.5, p. 15 (the two triples (Z,1,2) and (Z,2,1))

items.name: Family of canonical coverings
items.statement: For an Enriques family f:Y→S, set P=Pic^τ_{Y/S}, G=P^D. The inclusion P→Pic gives [X]∈H⁰(S,R¹f_*G_Y); a canonical covering family is a G_Y-torsor whose cohomology class maps to [X].

tests.name: FamilyofcanonicalcoveringsTest1
tests.statement: A section of f kills the obstruction.

tests.name: FamilyofcanonicalcoveringsTest2
tests.statement: Two covers differ by a pulled-back G-torsor from S.

tests.name: FamilyofcanonicalcoveringsTest3
tests.statement: Existence of a local cover alone does not identify it with a chosen global cover.

items.name: Canonical-cover obstruction
items.statement: For an Enriques family the exact sequence 0→H¹(S,G)→H¹(Y,G_Y)→H⁰(S,R¹f_*G_Y)→H²(S,G)→H²(Y,G_Y) makes the image of [X] the obstruction to a canonical cover.
items.note: Review note: Statement correct. The cohomology in sequence (2) must be fppf cohomology (G is μ₂ or α₂ in characteristic 2, not smooth); the paper does not say so, and the node should. It needs f_*(G_𝔜)=G, which holds because O_S→f_*O_𝔜 is an isomorphism universally for an Enriques family.

items.name: Injective pullback criterion for a canonical cover
items.statement: For an Enriques family over S=Spec R with P=Pic^τ and G=P^D, a canonical-cover family exists if H²(S,G)→H²(Y,G_Y) is injective.

items.name: Section criterion for a canonical cover
items.statement: For an Enriques family over S=Spec R with P=Pic^τ and G=P^D, a canonical-cover family exists if f admits a section.

items.name: Étale Picard torsion criterion for a canonical cover
items.statement: For an Enriques family over S=Spec R with P=Pic^τ and G=P^D, a canonical-cover family exists if P→S is étale and Pic(S)=0.

items.name: Twisting of canonical coverings
items.statement: When a canonical-cover family exists, its isomorphism classes form a torsor under H¹(S,G), acting by pullback and twisting.

items.name: Constant and split Picard schemes
items.statement: For an Enriques family, constant Num means Num≅Z¹⁰_S; constant Picard means Pic≅(Z/2×Z¹⁰)_S. Split Picard means the extension 0→Pic^τ→Pic→Num→0 splits.
api: splitting by lifts of a numerical basis

tests.name: ConstantandsplitPicardschemesTest1
tests.statement: Constant full Picard implies constant Num.

tests.name: ConstantandsplitPicardschemesTest2
tests.statement: An extension by Z/2 splits if every basis element lifts to a section.

tests.name: ConstantandsplitPicardschemesTest3
tests.statement: Constant Num alone does not force Pic^τ to be the constant Z/2 group.

items.name: Constant Picard scheme over Z
items.statement: Every Enriques family over Z has constant full Picard scheme.
items.note: Use /63’s four-twist repair and local scheme models before invoking Fontaine. Num constancy is established first from /180–/181; it does not depend on /62. Once μ₂ is excluded, finite étale Z/2-torsors above each numerical basis vector split over Z.

items.name: Canonical-cover compatibility at two
items.statement: If Y/Z is an Enriques family with Pic^τ=μ₂, then for any canonical double cover X of Y over Z[1/2], one of its twists by 1,−1,2,−2 has a generic K3 fiber admitting a smooth proper projective scheme model over Z_p for every prime p. In particular it has the required good reduction over W(F₂bar) at 2.
items.note: Previously unverified comparison now has an explicit mathematical proof in the report, assembled from /172–/188 and /54–/60,/79–/80. Choose a Z₂-cover first, correct its Q₂-difference by the globally supported twist, and extend the residual unramified class 5. The proof is proposed for independent review, not a Lean verification. Arbitrary global and local covers need not coincide. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The statement is the repaired step of the proof of Proposition 5.5 (E6), not a printed result. Checked step by step. (1) Over Z[1/2] the canonical covers are exactly the four twists of one of them: H¹(Z[1/2],Z/2)=H¹(Z[1/2],μ₂)=Z[1/2]^×/squares={1,−1,2,−2}, since Pic(Z[1/2])=0. (2) Over Z₂ a canonical cover X₂ exists (/177). (3) Over Q₂ the two canonical covers differ by c∈Q₂^×/Q₂^{×2}=⟨−1,2,5⟩ (/178). (4) u=(−1)^e2^a is the unique u∈{1,−1,2,−2} with cu∈{1,5}. The class 5 has the finite étale Z₂-model B of /175 (/179). (5) At odd p the Z_p-model is the base change of the twisted Z[1/2]-cover, and at p=2 it is X₂ twisted by B^b. Each is finite étale over Y_{Z_p}, which is a projective scheme by /184, so each is a smooth projective Z_p-scheme. Twisting does not change the geometric generic fibre, so the generic fibre is a K3 surface over Q. Fontaine's Theorem 1 with Remark (a) (scan p. 3: 'il existe un schéma propre et lisse Y sur Z_p tel que Y⊗Q_p = X⊗Q_p') then gives h^{2,0}=0, a contradiction. Remarks. The B-twist is needed only for a Z₂-model: over W(F̄₂) the class 5 is a square, so X₂⊗W(F̄₂) already works. The difference class over Frac W(F̄₂) is the image of c, so the paper's own route through A can also be closed by the same global twist.

items.name: Canonical covers with constant Picard
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Canonical-cover families exist, and their isomorphism classes form a torsor under R×/(R×)².
items.note: Review note: Statement faithful. The paper never defines Br(R). Its suppressed draft (TeX line 1282, inside an \iffalse block) sets Br(R)=H²(S,G_m). For the canonical-cover part of the theorem, the Azumaya Brauer group suffices, because H²(S,μ₂)→H²(S,G_m)[2]⊂H²(S,G_m)_tors=Br(S) for affine S (Gabber). Part (ii), /66, needs H²(S,G_m)=0; see /66.

items.name: Canonical bundle order
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. ω_{Y_k} has order 2 in Pic(Y_k).

items.name: Descent of numerical classes
items.statement: Let f:𝔜→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant Picard scheme, with Pic(R)=0 and H²_ét(Spec R,G_m)=0 (written Br(R)=0). For a homomorphism R→k to a field, every class l∈Num_{Y/k}(k̄) is the numerical class of an invertible sheaf L on Y=𝔜⊗_R k, unique up to tensoring with ω_Y. The same reading of Br(R)=0 applies to /67–/70.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: The hypothesis 'Br(R)=0' is ambiguous. The proof of (ii) kills the Leray obstruction Pic_{𝔜/R}(R)→H²(Spec R,G_m), so it needs H²_ét(Spec R,G_m)=0, the cohomological Brauer group of the author's suppressed draft. For a non-regular affine R, H²(Spec R,G_m) can be larger than the Azumaya Brauer group, and the item should pin the convention. For R=Z, and for fields, the two agree.

items.name: Descent of (-2)-curves
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Every (-2)-curve on Y_kbar descends to a (-2)-curve on Y_k isomorphic to P¹_k.

items.name: Descent of genus-one fibrations
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Every genus-one fibration Y_kbar→P¹_kbar descends to Y_k→P¹_k.

items.name: Rational tame double fibers
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Every descended genus-one fibration has exactly two multiple fibers, both tame, over k-rational base points.

items.name: Existence over the residue field
items.statement: Let f:Y→Spec R be an Enriques family with constant full Picard scheme and Pic(R)=Br(R)=0; for any R→k, write Y_k and Y_kbar for its fibers. Y_k has at least one genus-one fibration to P¹_k.

items.name: Rational Jacobian Weierstrass model
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. Contract all vertical curves disjoint from E to the normal Weierstrass model Z; over k[t] its equation is y²+a₁xy+a₃y=x³+a₂x²+a₄x+a₆, with deg a_i≤i; over k[t⁻¹] use a′_i=a_i/t^i.
items.locator: Proposition 6.1, p. 18 (statement and proof both on p. 18)

tests.name: RationalJacobianWeierstrassmodelTest1
tests.statement: The coefficient a₆ transforms by t⁻⁶.

tests.name: RationalJacobianWeierstrassmodelTest2
tests.statement: A reducible fiber can be contracted on Z even though J is smooth.

tests.name: RationalJacobianWeierstrassmodelTest3
tests.statement: O_J(3E) is not relatively very ample on a vertical component disjoint from E; the embedding concerns Z.

items.note: Review note: Statement correct. The coordinate paragraph of the proof mixes the two charts (see the amended E7); the conclusion a′ᵢ = aᵢ/tⁱ is right. Owner: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces (part-ii route).

items.name: Canonical sheaf and zero-section on a rational Jacobian
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. ω_J=φ*O(-1), E²=−1, and ω_{J/P¹}=φ*O(1).

items.name: Weierstrass pushforward splitting
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. φ_*O_J(3E)≅O⊕O(-2)⊕O(-3); the relative Proj construction gives the cubic equation of the Weierstrass model.
items.note: Review note: Correct; the relatively very ample sheaf is O_Z(3E) on the Weierstrass model, not O_J(3E) (E8).

items.name: Nonconstant rational-surface coefficients
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. In such a degree-bounded Weierstrass equation some a_i is nonconstant and some a_i is not divisible by t^i; these conditions survive degree-preserving admissible coordinate changes.
items.note: Source statement retained; minimality/rationality hypotheses are essential. Review note: Correct. The two conditions say exactly that the Weierstrass equation is minimal at t=∞ (some aᵢ non-constant, i.e. not all a′ᵢ divisible by sⁱ) and at t=0. The paper's reason is right once read with a coordinate change: if every aᵢ is divisible by tⁱ, then x=t²x′, y=t³y′ gives constant coefficients, the generic fibre is constant, and the relatively minimal model is P¹×E₀, which is not rational.

items.name: Jacobian of an Enriques genus-one fibration
items.statement: For an Enriques surface Y/k and genus-one fibration with generic fiber Y_η over K=k(t), use Pic⁰_{Y_η/K} in the elliptic case, and its unique regular compactification in the quasielliptic case; its relatively minimal regular surface model J→P¹ is the Jacobian fibration with zero-section.

tests.name: JacobianofanEnriquesgenusonefibrationTest1
tests.statement: The elliptic generic Jacobian is an elliptic curve.

tests.name: JacobianofanEnriquesgenusonefibrationTest2
tests.statement: The quasielliptic Pic⁰ is a form of G_a and needs compactification.

tests.name: JacobianofanEnriquesgenusonefibrationTest3
tests.statement: One must not treat a quasielliptic generic fiber as a smooth elliptic curve.

items.name: Rationality of the Enriques Jacobian
items.statement: The regular Jacobian surface of a genus-one fibration on an Enriques surface over any field is geometrically rational.
items.note: Review note: Correct. The proof's ψ⁻¹(V) should read φ⁻¹(V) (E9).

items.name: Algebraic-cycle zeta formula
items.statement: Let X/F_q be smooth proper with H⁰(O_X)=F_q, and ℓ≠char F_q. If H^{2j+1}(Xbar,Q_ℓ)=0 for every j≥0 and the BASE-FIELD cycle map CH^j(X)⊗Q_ℓ→H^{2j}(Xbar,Q_ℓ(j)) is surjective for every j≥0, then Z(X,T)=∏_j(1−q^jT)^(−b_{2j}).
items.note: Cycles on Xbar alone do not imply trivial Frobenius on the twisted group.

items.name: Algebraic-cycle point-count formula
items.statement: Let X/F_q be smooth proper with H⁰(O_X)=F_q, and ℓ≠char F_q. Under the preceding odd-vanishing and base-defined-cycle-surjectivity hypotheses, #X(F_{q^r})=Σ_j b_{2j}q^{jr} for every r≥1.
items.locator: Proposition 7.1, formula (9), p. 20. The paper states only r=1; the formula for every r follows by taking logarithms of (9): N_r = Σ_j b_{2j} q^{jr}.
items.note: The r=1 formula is displayed; r≥1 follows by retaining the same Frobenius eigenvalues.

items.name: Surface count from constant Num
items.statement: Let X/F_q be smooth proper with H⁰(O_X)=F_q, and ℓ≠char F_q. If X is a surface with b₁=0, b₂=ρ and constant Num_{X/F_q}, then #X(F_q)=1+b₂q+q².
items.note: Correct the printed F_p to F_q; b₃=0 follows by duality. Review note: Correct with F_q (E11). The proof also misprints b₃=0 as b₁=0 (new issue below).

items.name: Twenty-five points over F₂
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper surface over F_q with h⁰(O_X)=1 that is either an Enriques surface or a geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal genus-one fibration X→P¹. If the local system Num_{X/F_q} is constant, then #X(F_q)=1+10q+q². In particular #X(F₂)=25.
items.locator: Corollary 7.3 and the sentence after it, p. 21
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Corollary 7.3 is stated over an arbitrary finite field F_q, with #X(F_q)=1+10q+q². The value 25 is the case q=2, from the sentence after the corollary. The item keeps only that case.

items.name: Isogeny for multiple fibers
items.statement: Let R be an excellent DVR with fraction field F and residue field k, let E/R be an elliptic scheme, and let X/R be the relatively minimal regular model of a torsor under E_F whose reduced special fiber is an elliptic curve. The elliptic curves E_k and (X_k)_red are isogenous over k.

items.name: Multiple-fiber extension counts
items.statement: Let R be an excellent DVR with fraction field F and residue field k, let E/R be an elliptic scheme, and let X/R be the relatively minimal regular model of a torsor under E_F whose reduced special fiber is an elliptic curve. If k=F_q, then #E_k(F_{q^r})=#X_k(F_{q^r}) for every r≥1.

items.name: Multiple-fiber isomorphism over F₂
items.statement: Let R be an excellent DVR with fraction field F and residue field k, let E/R be an elliptic scheme, and let X/R be the relatively minimal regular model of a torsor under E_F whose reduced special fiber is an elliptic curve. If k=F₂, then E_k≅(X_k)_red over F₂.

items.name: Genus under domination of an elliptic curve
items.statement: For any field k, an integral proper k-curve C with a dominant morphism to an elliptic curve E/k satisfies h¹(O_C)≥1.

items.name: Regularity in the genus-one equality case
items.statement: In the preceding situation, h¹(O_C)=1 implies that C is regular.
items.note: Do not strengthen regular to smooth over an imperfect field without proof.

items.name: Quotient models of multiple fibers
items.statement: Let R contain a residue-field representative k, let A/k be an abelian variety, G⊂A(k) a finite subgroup, and F′/Frac R a G-Galois extension whose integral closure R′ has the same residue field k. The free diagonal action gives X=(A×Spec R′)/G, with generic fiber a form of A and reduced special fiber A/G.

tests.name: QuotientmodelsofmultiplefibersTest1
tests.statement: For G=0 the model is A_R.

tests.name: QuotientmodelsofmultiplefibersTest2
tests.statement: The reduced special fiber is the quotient by translations.

tests.name: QuotientmodelsofmultiplefibersTest3
tests.statement: The multiple fiber must not be identified with its reduction as a scheme.

items.name: Constant Picard of the Jacobian
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. J has constant Picard scheme.

items.name: Matching geometric Kodaira types
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. At every geometric point over a closed point a∈P¹, the underlying indecomposable fibers of Y and J have the same Kodaira symbol.
items.note: Use Liu–Lorenzini–Raynaud 6.6 after passage to algebraically closed residue field, keeping multiplicity separate. Review note: LLR Theorem 6.6 checked in the authors' PDF (Invent. Math. 157 (2004), p. 496): k algebraically closed, m the order of the torsor class in H¹(K,E_K). The proof of Proposition 9.2 passes to the strict henselization of O_{P¹,a}, whose residue field F̄₂ is algebraically closed, so the hypothesis holds.

items.name: Simple-fiber identification
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. If Y_a is simple, J_a≅Y_a over κ(a).
items.note: For the smooth-locus point in Proposition 9.2, distinguish tree-shaped additive fibers (choose a multiplicity-one terminal component) from I_n cycles. A cycle has no terminal component; choose any component and remove its at most two intersection points. Over F₂ a rational P¹ still has a smooth point. Nonsplit I₁/I₂ use their conductor descriptions. This is a proof clarification, not a new fiber-isomorphism assertion. Review note: The note's smooth-point repair (E12) misses type IV. The dual graph of IV is a triangle under the paper's Section 2 definition, so it has no terminal vertex. Any component of IV meets the other two in a single point, which leaves two rational points in the smooth locus. For additive fibres the chosen component must also have multiplicity one. The printed 'regular locus of C_red' is not enough.

items.name: Nonrational fibers
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. Every geometric fiber of J over a non-F₂-rational closed point of P¹ is irreducible.

items.name: Excluded I₀*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. No geometric fiber of J is of type I₀*.

items.name: Semistable graph descent
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. For every semistable geometric fiber, Γ(J_ā)→Γ(J_a) is an isomorphism.

items.name: At most one semistable or supersingular rational fiber
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. At most one a∈P¹(F₂) has J_a semistable or smooth supersingular.
items.note: Review note: Statement correct. The proof's step from the multiple fibre of Y to J_b needs Corollary 8.3, not only the Kodaira symbols of Proposition 9.2 (new gap below).

items.name: Descent of all Mordell–Weil sections
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme, ϕ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and φ:J→P¹ its relatively minimal Jacobian. MW(J/P¹)=MW(Jbar/P¹bar).
items.note: The printed Br(F₂(t))=0 is false. Proposed repair uses Tsen over F₂bar(t) and the Galois-equivariant quotient of geometric Picard; see report. Review note: The repair recorded in the note and in E13 is correct. Pic(Ȳ)→MW(J̄/P̄¹), L↦(L−(deg(L|Y_F̄)/2)R)|Y_F̄, is surjective by Tsen over F̄₂(t) and Galois-equivariant. Galois-fixed points of J(F̄₂(t)) are J(F₂(t)).

items.name: Fiber-count input for Picard descent
items.statement: For a rational Jacobian elliptic surface over F₂ and a rational base point a, let r_a be its geometric component count. Put n_a=i for smooth E_i, 2r_a for split semistable, 2r_a+2 for nonsplit semistable, and 2r_a+1 for unstable fiber. This is a formal input until splitting is proved.
api: sum over three rational base points

tests.name: FibercountinputforPicarddescentTest1
tests.statement: For a split I₄ fiber n_a=8.

tests.name: FibercountinputforPicarddescentTest2
tests.statement: For a nonsplit I₂ fiber n_a=6.

tests.name: FibercountinputforPicarddescentTest3
tests.statement: Before graph descent, n_a is not automatically the actual point count of J_a.

items.name: Picard constancy criterion for rational elliptic surfaces
items.statement: Let J be a smooth geometrically rational surface over F₂ with a relatively minimal jacobian elliptic fibration φ:J→P¹. Assume: (i) J_ā is irreducible for every closed non-rational a; (ii) no J_ā has Kodaira symbol I₀*; (iii) if J_ā is semistable, Γ(J_ā)→Γ(J_a) is a graph isomorphism; (iv) at most one rational b∈P¹ has J_b semistable or smooth supersingular; (v) MW(J/P¹)=MW(J̄/P̄¹); and Σ_{a∈P¹(F₂)} n_a=25. Then Pic_{J/F₂} is constant.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: The phrase 'every semistable fiber has split component graph' could be read as 'split semistable', which would wrongly exclude Ĩ₁ and Ĩ₂. Condition (iii) of Proposition 9.3 asks that Γ(J_ā)→Γ(J_a) be a graph isomorphism whenever J_ā is semistable. Review note: Hypotheses (iv) and Σn_a=25 are part of Theorem 9.4 as printed, but its proof (through Proposition 9.5) uses only (i), (ii), (iii) and (v).

items.name: Additive graph rigidity
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be as in Theorem 9.4 and satisfy conditions (ii), (iii) and (v) of Proposition 9.3. Then for every rational a∈P¹ with J_a singular, Γ(J_ā)→Γ(J_a) is a graph isomorphism.
items.note: The claim in the proof that orthogonal projection preserves the pairing is not used. Report supplies a dual-lattice argument requiring review. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Same ambiguous wording ('split component graph') as /96. The added hypothesis Σn_a=25 is harmless but is not used; the proof uses only (ii), (iii) and (v). Review note: The dual-lattice repair of E14 is correct. The proof has two further slips about terminal vertices: IV is not a tree, and III* and II* have two further terminal vertices (new issues below).

items.name: Even unimodular complement for a rational Jacobian
items.statement: Let J/k be a smooth geometrically rational surface with a relatively minimal Jacobian genus-one fibration φ:J→P¹ and zero-section E. Over an algebraic closure, the orthogonal complement W of the fiber F and zero-section O in Num(Jbar) is even unimodular of rank 8; it is generated by vertical components disjoint from O and (P−O)−(1+P·O)F for sections P.
items.note: The span of F,O has Gram matrix [[0,1],[1,-1]]; the geometric statement is not supplied by abstract lattice APIs. Review note: Correct. W is negative definite (it lies in the orthogonal complement of a hyperbolic-type plane inside Num of signature (1,9)), so W≅E₈(−1).

items.name: Geometric torsor Kodaira comparison
items.statement: Let R be a DVR with algebraically closed residue field, C/K a smooth geometrically connected genus-one curve of period m, E/K its Jacobian, and X,E_min their proper regular minimal models. If E_min has Kodaira type T, then X has type mT.
items.note: Statement and proof read. Do not apply without algebraically closed residue field: their Remark 6.8 warns it fails more generally. The 2018 corrigendum corrects §4 Brauer formulas, not the statement of 6.6. Review note: Statement checked against the authors' PDF of LLR 2004, Theorem 6.6, p. 496, including the definition of m as the period.

items.name: Existence of a large rational fiber
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. Some rational fiber has at least six irreducible components.
acceptance: Assuming every component count≤5 gives at most 10+7+7=24 points, contrary to 25.

items.name: Existence of a reducible additive fiber
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. There is a reducible unstable fiber over a rational base point.
items.note: Review note: Confirmed by the exhaustive search (see /115): every class satisfying the hypotheses has a reducible unstable rational fibre. Lang's exclusion of II+I₉ is consistent with the computation.

items.name: Unique additive fiber for nonzero functional j

items.note: The intermediate c₄ criterion needs Δ=0; a smooth supersingular fiber is not additive. Review note: Confirmed by the exhaustive search. The c₄ criterion needs Δ(x)=0 (E15).

items.name: Small additive fiber configuration
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. If j≠0 and the unique unstable fiber has at most five components, the rational-fiber configuration, up to a base automorphism, is III+E₄+I₈.
items.note: Review note: Confirmed by the exhaustive search: III+E₄+I₈ is the only class with j≠0 whose unstable fibre has at most five components.

items.name: Classification with nonzero functional j
items.statement: Let J be a smooth geometrically rational surface over F₂ with a relatively minimal jacobian elliptic fibration φ:J→P¹, constant Picard scheme, and at most one rational point whose fibre is semistable or smooth supersingular. If the functional j-invariant is non-zero, then up to coordinate changes and automorphisms of P¹ the fibration is given by exactly one of eleven Weierstrass equations. The eight of Theorem 10.4 are: y²+txy+t²y=x³+tx²+t⁴x+t⁵(1+t) [I₁*+E₄+I₄, j=t⁴]; y²+txy=x³+t³x+t⁵(1+t) [III*+E₄+E₄, j=t²/(t²+t+1)]; y²+txy=x³+t³x [III*+E₄+I₂, j=t²]; y²+txy=x³+t²x²+t³x [III*+E₂+Ĩ₂, j=t²]; y²+txy=x³+t⁵ [II*+E₄+I₁, j=t]; y²+txy=x³+t²x²+t⁵ [II*+E₂+Ĩ₁, j=t]; y²+txy=x³+tx²+t⁴x [I₄*+E₂+E₄, j=1]; y²+txy+ty=x³+tx²+tx [III+E₄+I₈, j=t⁸]. The three further ones are: y²+txy+t³y=x³+x² [I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, Δ=t¹⁰, j=t²]; y²+txy+t³y=x³+tx² [I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁, Δ=t¹¹, j=t]; y²+txy+t²y=x³+t²x² [IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂, Δ=t⁸(t²+t+1), j=t⁴/(t²+t+1)]. Fibres are listed over t=0, 1, ∞. The non-rational fibres are smooth except for an I₁ fibre over the point t²+t+1=0 in the models with j=t²/(t²+t+1) and j=t⁴/(t²+t+1).
items.note: Full Lang 2000 classification proof not acquired; finite invariant checks do not establish exhaustiveness. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: False as stated: the list of Theorem 10.4 is incomplete (new issue below). An exhaustive search shows three more isomorphism classes with j≠0 that satisfy the hypotheses: I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁ and IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂. The search ran over all 2²¹ Weierstrass equations, normalised to a₂=0, then modulo the 512 coordinate changes and PGL₂(F₂). The printed eight are each unique in their configuration. Review note: The route briefs must be corrected: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces says 'eight nonzero-j and three zero-j models', and EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence says '11-model classification' and '15→8→0 configuration reductions'. Condition (i) is equivalent to #J(F₂)=25 for geometrically rational J (trace of Frobenius on NS equals 10). This makes Theorems 10.4 and 10.5 a finite computation over F₂ that needs Tate's algorithm but not Lang 2000; the classification should be planned that way (new coverage item).

items.name: Nonrational fibers of the eight nonzero-j models
items.statement: For the eight models of Theorem 10.4, all fibers at nonrational base points are smooth except in the j=t²/(t²+t+1) model, which has an I₁ fiber at the unique degree-two point t²+t+1=0.
items.note: Review note: True for the eight printed models (verified). In the corrected classification (/115), the added model IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂ also has an I₁ fibre over t²+t+1=0.

items.name: Classification with zero functional j
items.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. If j=0, exactly one of the three models in Theorem 10.5 represents the fibration up to admissible coordinate changes and base automorphisms.
items.note: Review note: Confirmed by the exhaustive search: with a₁=0 exactly three classes satisfy (i) and (ii), the three printed. Five more j=0 classes have constant Picard scheme but violate (ii), since they have two smooth supersingular rational fibres (e.g. y²+y=x³+t: II*+E₃+E₃, 25 points).

items.name: Nonrational fibers of zero-j models
items.statement: All fibers at nonrational base points in the three models of Theorem 10.5 are smooth.
items.note: Review note: Verified (Δ=t⁸ in all three models; no other zeros).

items.name: Elliptic configurations on constant-Picard Enriques surfaces
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For an elliptic fibration, up to base automorphism the rational-fiber types are exactly among II*+E₄+I₁; II*+E₂+nonsplit I₁; III*+E₄+I₂; III*+E₂+nonsplit I₂; III*+E₄+E₄; IV*+E₃+IV; IV*+E₅+III; I₄*+E₄+E₂; I₁*+E₅+IV; I₁*+E₄+I₄; III+E₄+I₈.
items.locator: Proposition 11.1 and table (12), pp. 32–33 (the proposition begins on p. 32, the table is on p. 33); proof pp. 33–34
items.note: Necessary possibilities, not assertions that all are realized by Enriques surfaces; the paper ultimately excludes the nonexceptional surfaces. Review note: Checked against the TeX: the eleven elliptic entries (with ˜I₁, ˜I₂ the non-split semistable fibres and E_i the elliptic curve over F₂ with i points, i.e. J_a≅Y_a or J_a≅(Y_a)_red) agree exactly. No atlas stage plans it; missing is right.

items.name: Quasielliptic configurations
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For a quasielliptic fibration, the three rational fibers have types among II*+II+II; III*+III+II; I₄*+II+II; I₂*+III+III, up to base automorphism.
items.note: Review note: Checked: the only solutions of r₀+r₁+r_∞=11 with r∈{1,2,7,8,9} are 9+1+1, 8+2+1, 7+2+2, which with II* and I₄* both having 9 components give exactly the four listed configurations.

items.name: Quasielliptic component sum
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For a quasielliptic fibration, r₀+r₁+r_∞=11. Its possible fiber symbols are II,III,I₂*,III*,II*,I₄*, with respective component counts 1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 9.
items.note: The generic degree-zero Picard group is killed by 2; imports the quasielliptic classification, not yet fully source-extracted. Review note: Uses /197 (Pic⁰ of the generic fibre is 2-torsion, so ρ=2+Σ(r_a−1)) and /19 (no I₀*); I_{2n}* with n≥3 has at least 11 components and is excluded by the sum. Correct.

items.name: Forced multiple fibers
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. Every IV, IV*, II*, or I₁* fiber of a genus-one fibration is multiple.
items.note: Review note: Checked the proof (p. 34): in each table entry containing IV, IV*, II* or I₁* the third rational fibre is semistable (I₁, ˜I₁, I₄) or supersingular (E₃, E₅), so by /36 and /69 the two multiple fibres are the other two rational fibres; quasi-elliptic II* uses /43.

items.name: Simple III* preliminary restriction
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. If a genus-one fibration has a simple III* fiber, it is elliptic and its rational-fiber configuration is III*+E₄+E₄.
items.note: Review note: Uses /43 (quasi-elliptic excluded) and /36 (III*+E₄+I₂ and III*+E₂+˜I₂ would force III* to be multiple). Correct.

items.name: Excluded rational two-section for exceptional-type half-fibers
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For a multiple fiber of type IV*, III*, or II*, there is no (-2)-curve R with R·F_ind=1.
items.note: Review note: Direct translation of /44 (a (−2)-curve R with R·φ⁻¹_ind(a)=1 is a two-section). Correct.

items.name: Elimination of I₈
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration on Y has a fibre of type I₈. (Every application, in Propositions 11.3 and 11.4, is to nonexceptional surfaces. Alternatively keep the paper's generality and prove the partner fibration from the new Cossec–Dolgachev Theorem 3.4.1 coverage item: it exists unless Ȳ is extra-special of type Ẽ₈. The ten (−2)-curves of such a surface form the tree T_{2,3,7} (arXiv:2201.05481, Definition 1.1), so it has no I₈ fibre.)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Missing hypothesis relative to the proof. The paper's Proposition 11.2 says only 'Assumption as in Proposition 11.1', but its proof (p. 34) needs a genus-one fibration ψ whose half-fibre F has F·φ⁻¹_ind(0)=1, i.e. Proposition 4.4(iii) (/45), which the paper and the extraction state only for NONEXCEPTIONAL surfaces in characteristic 2. As extracted, /125 cannot be proved from the extraction's items. See the new sourceIssue on Proposition 11.2. Review note: Proof re-checked step by step (pp. 34–35): the reduction to ψ with configuration III+E₄+I₈ and the final I₃/I₇ contradiction are correct. Depends on /36, /45, /69, /119.

items.name: Elimination of II*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a fiber of type II*.
items.locator: Proposition 11.3, p. 35; proof pp. 36–38 (II* case and multiple I₄* case p. 36, IV* case p. 37, IV case pp. 37–38)
items.note: Review note: II* case checked: C₁+⋯+C₈ is E₈=T_{2,3,5}, so ψ⁻¹(∞) is II*, multiple by /122, and (C₀+2C₈)·R≥2 contradicts φ⁻¹_ind·ψ⁻¹_ind=1.

items.name: Elimination of IV*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a fiber of type IV*.
items.locator: Proposition 11.3, p. 35; proof pp. 36–38 (II* case and multiple I₄* case p. 36, IV* case p. 37, IV case pp. 37–38)
items.note: Review note: IV* case checked, including the four rational points on C′₀≅P¹_{F₂} (it uses /125, so it inherits /125's nonexceptional hypothesis, which holds here).

items.name: Elimination of IV
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a fiber of type IV.
items.locator: Proposition 11.3, p. 35; proof pp. 36–38 (II* case and multiple I₄* case p. 36, IV* case p. 37, IV case pp. 37–38)
items.note: Review note: IV case: see the two new sourceIssues on p. 38 (φ⁻¹_ind(∞) printed for φ⁻¹_ind(0), and the omitted case in which C′₁+C′₂ lies in ψ⁻¹(∞) itself). Both are repaired by an intersection count, so the statement stands.

items.name: No multiple I₄*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a multiple I₄* fiber.
items.locator: Proposition 11.3, p. 35; proof pp. 36–38 (II* case and multiple I₄* case p. 36, IV* case p. 37, IV case pp. 37–38)
