items.name: Eight residual configurations
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. Any genus-one fibration has, up to base automorphism, one of these rational-fiber configurations: elliptic I₄*+E₄+E₂, III*+E₄+I₂, III*+E₂+nonsplit I₂, III*+E₄+E₄, I₁*+E₄+I₄; quasielliptic I₄*+II+II, III*+III+II, I₂*+III+III.
items.note: Review note: Checked: removing every configuration with II*, IV*, IV or I₈ from table (12) leaves exactly these eight ('from fifteen to eight', p. 34).

items.name: Multiplicity restrictions in the residual table
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For any genus-one fibration, every I₁* fiber is multiple; fibers of type I₄*, I_n, and nonsplit I₂ are simple.
items.note: Review note: I₁* multiple by /122; I₄* simple by /129; I_n and ˜I₂ simple by /36 and /69. Correct.

items.name: Partner fibration over F₂
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For every genus-one fibration ϕ there is ψ:Y→P¹ over F₂ with intersection ϕ⁻¹(∞)·ψ⁻¹(∞)=4.
items.note: Review note: Paper derives it from Proposition 4.4(iii) (/45) over F̄₂; descent of the partner fibration to F₂ is /68.

items.name: Elimination of I₄*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a fiber of type I₄*.
items.locator: Proposition 12.1, p. 38; proof pp. 38–40 (it uses Propositions 12.2 and 12.3, pp. 41–44)
items.note: Review note: All six cases of the proof were re-checked against the Kodaira graphs and multiplicities. They are correct as written; the III*-subcase of F·C₀=F·C₈=1 and the I₂*-subcase of F·C₂=1 reduce to /135, and the F·C₀=2 case reduces to /139.

items.name: Six I₄* half-fiber incidence cases
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. If a simple I₄* fiber has components C₀,C₁ meeting C₂, chain C₂—C₃—C₄—C₅—C₆, and C₇,C₈ meeting C₆, then a half-fiber F of a partner fibration with F·(I₄* fiber)=2 has, up to graph symmetry, one of: F·C₂=1; F·C₃=1; F·C₄=1; F·C₀=F·C₁=1; F·C₀=F·C₈=1; F·C₀=2; unspecified intersections are 0.
items.note: The report’s exact orbit check enumerates 15 nonnegative incidence vectors of weighted degree 2 and obtains precisely the six listed graph-symmetry orbits. It does not prove realization or exclusion of those cases. Review note: Recomputed independently: 15 nonnegative vectors (a₀,…,a₈) with a₀+a₁+a₇+a₈+2(a₂+⋯+a₆)=2, forming 6 orbits under the order-8 symmetry group of D̃₈. The orbit list is correct.

items.name: First forbidden ten-curve configuration
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. There is no simple-normal-crossing configuration of ten (-2)-curves C₀,…,C₈,R with affine D₈ graph C₀,C₁—C₂—C₃—C₄—C₅—C₆—C₇,C₈ and with R meeting only C₄ once.
items.locator: Proposition 12.2 and dual graph (13), p. 41; proof pp. 41–42
items.note: The comma notation denotes forks at C₂ and C₆, not edges C₀—C₁ or C₇—C₈.

items.name: First ten-curve lattice discriminant
items.statement: In the hypothetical configuration of Proposition 12.2, S=⟨C₁,…,C₈,R,F⟩, with F a half-fiber of the I₄* fibration, has determinant−4 and index 2 in Num(Y); S*/S≅(Z/2)². The vector class represented by C₁* has norm−1 mod 2Z, and the two spinor classes C₇*,C₈* have norm−2 mod 2Z.
items.note: Full-norm mod 2Z is the paper convention. Built Tau Ceti uses half-norm modZ; translate, do not redefine the discriminant API. Review note: Recomputed in exact rational arithmetic (S/rv4_lattice.py): Gram matrix N as in the Magma comment (basis C₁,…,C₈,R,F; R·C₄=R·F=1, F²=0), det N=−4, signature (1,9), elementary divisors 1⁸,2,2, and N⁻¹ equal entry by entry to the printed matrix (14). The dual vectors outside S are C₁*,C₃*,C₅*,C₇*,C₈*, with C₁*≡C₃*≡C₅*≡C₇*+C₈* mod S, (C₁*)²=−1, (C₇*)²=(C₈*)²=−2, C₇*·C₈*=−3/2, C₁*·C₇*=C₁*·C₈*=−1/2. In Tau Ceti's half-norm convention (/155) the vector class has q=1/2 and the spinor classes q=0 mod Z. Index 2 follows from /159 or /160 applied to S⊂Num(Y) with Num(Y) unimodular (/29).

items.name: Two-section of square zero or minus two
items.statement: In the lattice argument of Proposition 12.2, the nontrivial generic Picard quotient supplies an integral two-section R̃ with R̃²∈{0,−2}; the proof must apply the Enriques Reducibility Theorem, not assume R̃ is a rational curve.
items.note: Review note: Correct as stated. Over F₂ the reducibility step (/210) should be applied on Ȳ; the resulting (−2)-curve, or the fibration with half-fibre R̃, descends by /67–/69 (multiple fibres lie over rational points), which the final rational-point count needs. See also the new sourceIssue on the 'R̃≡C₈*' step, and the new coverage item on the incidences of R̃.

items.name: Square-zero two-section calculation
items.statement: In the square-zero branch of Proposition 12.2, after choosing the spinor lift, the two-section class is C₈*+nR*+F* with n≥0, and its square is 2n; hence n=0.
acceptance: Compute with the inverse of matrix(14); preserve the zero-square branch.
items.note: Review note: Verified: (C₈*)²=(F*)²=−2, (R*)²=C₈*·R*=0, C₈*·F*=2, R*·F*=1, so (C₈*+nR*+F*)²=2n. It presupposes R̃·C₀=R̃·C₈=1 and R̃·C_i=0 otherwise (R̃⊥C₁,…,C₇). The paper reaches this by an invalid 'without loss of generality' (new sourceIssue); the correct reduction uses the symmetries C₀↔C₁, C₇↔C₈ of (13).

items.name: Second forbidden ten-curve configuration
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. There is no configuration of ten (-2)-curves C₀,…,C₈,R whose C_i have affine D₈ incidence as above and with R·C₀=2, R·C₂=1, R·C_i=0 for other i. Require simple normal crossings away from the pair R,C₀.
items.locator: Proposition 12.3 and dual graph (15), p. 42; proof pp. 43–44
items.note: Do not impose simple normal crossings on the pair R,C₀: the intersection number is 2. Review note: Proof re-checked. Its reference to 'the proof of Proposition 12.1' uses only the case F·C₀=F·C₈=1 there, which rests on /135, not on /139, so there is no circularity.

items.name: Second ten-curve lattice discriminant
items.statement: For Proposition 12.3, the lattice S=⟨C₁,…,C₈,F′,F⟩ has Gram matrix D₈(-1)⊕U, determinant−4 and index 2 in Num(Y); its discriminant has two nonzero isotropic spinor classes and a vector class of odd full norm.
items.note: Review note: Recomputed (S/rv4_lattice.py): N=D₈(−1)⊕U, det −4, signature (1,9), elementary divisors 1⁸,2,2; N⁻¹ equals the printed (16) exactly; F*=F′, F′*=F; same discriminant classes and norms as for (14). The admissible incidences of R̃ were recomputed: only {C₀,C₇}, {C₀,C₈}, {C₁,C₇}, {C₁,C₈} give an isotropic nonzero class, matching the paper's two cases up to C₇↔C₈.

items.name: Generic degree-zero Picard quotient
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 12.3 (φ with simple fibre φ⁻¹(∞)=C₀+C₁+2(C₂+⋯+C₆)+C₇+C₈ and configuration I₄*+E₄+E₂ or I₄*+II+II, F a half-fibre of φ, F′ an integral half-fibre of φ′ with F·F′=1, S=⟨C₁,…,C₈,F′,F⟩⊂Num(Y)), the map L↦(L−(L·F)F′)|_{Y_K} induces an isomorphism Num(Y)/S ≅ Pic⁰(Y_K), where Y_K is the generic fibre of φ. Hence Pic⁰(Y_K) has order 2 and Pic(Y_K)=Pic⁰(Y_K)⊕Z·[F′_K]. The same holds in Proposition 12.2 with R in place of F′ and S=⟨C₁,…,C₈,R,F⟩.
items.note: The source displays Pic(Y_K); degree classes in 2Z are removed, so Pic⁰(Y_K) is the appropriate target. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Stated as a note about the misprint (E17) rather than as a mathematical statement; it does not say which lattice and which map. Review note: Needs the general generic-fibre item proposed under coverage (restriction is surjective, with kernel generated by vertical curves); ω_Y=O(F₁−F₂) restricts trivially, so the map factors through Num(Y).

items.name: Elimination of multiple III*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a multiple III* fiber.
items.note: Review note: Proof re-checked (pp. 44–45), including the use of /135 to force (R·C₆,R′·C₆)=(0,2) and the final 1=φ⁻¹_ind·ψ⁻¹_ind=2 contradiction.

items.name: Elimination of simple III*
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. No genus-one fibration has a simple III* fiber.
items.note: Review note: All four cases re-checked (pp. 45–47); each ends in /135, an I₆ or I₈ curve of canonical type, or the bound 'distinct fibrations meet with fibre product ≥4' (new coverage item).

items.name: Four simple III* half-fiber cases
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant full Picard scheme. For the simple III* component numbering of §13, a half-fiber F of a partner fibration has, up to symmetry, incidences F·C₂=1; or F·C₀=F·C₇=1; or F·C₁=1; or F·C₀=2, with all other intersections 0.
items.note: The report’s exact orbit check enumerates 6 nonnegative incidence vectors of weighted degree 2 and obtains precisely the four listed graph-symmetry orbits. The geometric contradiction within each branch still imports the source prerequisites. Review note: Recomputed independently: with III* multiplicities (C₀,C₁,C₂,C₃,C₄,C₅,C₆,C₇)=(1,2,2,3,4,3,2,1) there are 6 nonnegative vectors of weighted degree 2, forming 4 orbits under C₀↔C₇, C₁↔C₆, C₃↔C₅. Correct.

items.name: Final two-configuration impossibility
items.statement: Over any algebraically closed field, no classical Enriques surface has the configuration of reducible fibers of every genus-one fibration restricted to one of: I₁*+I₄ with the I₁* fiber multiple, or I₂*+III+III with two multiple fibers.
items.note: This last combinatorial theorem is not restricted to F₂. It first excludes I₁*, then multiple I₂*, then forces an excluded I₄ configuration. Review note: Statement faithful to the paper. The proof uses Ekedahl–Shepherd-Barron Theorem A (to get nonexceptional) and Proposition 4.4(iii) (/45), which is stated only for p=2; for p≠2 it needs Cossec–Dolgachev Theorem 3.4.1 directly (new sourceIssue, new coverage item). Theorem 15.1 applies it only to Ȳ over F̄₂, which is nonexceptional by hypothesis. So the roadmap can either add 'p=2 and Y nonexceptional' as a hypothesis, or import the general Cossec–Dolgachev item.

items.name: No nonexceptional constant-Picard Enriques surface over F₂
items.statement: There is no Enriques surface over F₂ which is both nonexceptional and has constant full Picard scheme.
items.locator: §15 and Theorem 15.1 with its proof, p. 49
items.note: Review note: Proof checked: every genus-one fibration of Ȳ descends (/68), non-rational fibres are irreducible and simple, and /130, /133, /142, /143 leave I₁*+E₄+I₄ (I₁* multiple) or I₂*+III+III (two multiple), which is the hypothesis of /145.

items.name: Low-degree off-diagonal Hodge vanishing
items.statement: Let X be a proper smooth variety over Q such that, for every prime p, there is a proper smooth scheme Z_p over W(F̄_p) with Z_p⊗Frac W(F̄_p)≅X⊗_Q Frac W(F̄_p). Then H^j(X,Ω_X^i)=0 whenever i≠j and i+j≤3. (Fontaine 1993, Theorem 1 and Remark (a); in particular this holds when X has a proper smooth Z_p-scheme model for every p.)
items.locator: §5, p. 16; Fontaine 1993 Theorem 1 and following remark(a)
items.note: The unramified Witt-ring version is essential; a theorem only for globally smooth proper Z-models is too weak for the stated application. Fontaine's theorem statement and remark were read visually, not its full proof. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: 'smooth proper model' must say scheme. Fontaine's Remark (a) (scan p. 3) asks, for every p, for 'Z propre et lisse sur W(F̄_p)' in the sense of a proper smooth scheme ('un schéma propre et lisse'), with Z⊗Frac W(F̄_p)=X⊗Frac W(F̄_p). The repair of E6 turns on exactly this point: an algebraic-space model is not enough as stated.

items.name: No everywhere-unramified-good K3 surface
items.statement: No K3 surface X/Q has good reduction over W(F_pbar) for every prime p: the preceding theorem would give h^{2,0}=0, but a K3 surface has h^{2,0}=1.
items.note: Review note: Statement correct, with 'good reduction' meaning a proper smooth scheme model over W(F̄_p) (see /147).

items.name: Characteristic-two Enriques lifting criterion
items.statement: For an Enriques surface Y over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 2, Y is exceptional or supersingular iff it has no flat proper lift to W₂(k).
items.locator: Schröer 2021 Theorem 7.2, author pp. 23–24; main paper Theorem 5.2
items.note: Review note: Checked against Schröer 2021b (Eur. J. Math. 7), §7, Theorem 7.2, (i)⇔(ii), with k algebraically closed; text read in the earlier worker's copy sch23-deligne-illusie.txt. Theorem 5.2 follows by base change Z/4→W₂(F̄₂). A flat deformation of a scheme over a nilpotent thickening is again a scheme, so the algebraic-space family causes no problem.

items.name: Miniversal Enriques deformation ring
items.statement: For such Y, its miniversal complete local deformation ring A is regular and W(k)-flat with dimension 11 or 12. Dimension 12, absolute ramification index at least 2, exceptionality-or-supersingularity, and nonexistence of a W₂ lift are equivalent.
items.note: Proof reads §6 criterion and prior deformation theorem; full prerequisite closure still outstanding. Review note: Matches Schröer 2021b Theorem 7.2: A is regular, 11≤dim A≤12, W-flat, and (i)–(iv) are equivalent. Uses Proposition 7.1 there (h¹(Θ_Y)=12 exactly for exceptional or supersingular surfaces).

items.name: Dual lattice is the span of the dual basis
items.statement: For a nondegenerate integral lattice L and finite Z-basis b, its dual carrier is the Z-span of the bilinear-dual basis of the corresponding Q-basis.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at Tau Ceti f790474: TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Dual/Basic.lean:85, dualCarrier_eq_span_dualBasis (L) [L.IsNondegenerate] (b : Basis ι ℤ L.carrier), L.dualCarrier = span ℤ (range (L.form.dualBasis … (b.extendOfIsLattice ℚ))). Matches the item; library is right.

items.name: Perfect lattice dual pairing
items.statement: For a nondegenerate integral lattice L, pairing gives a Z-linear equivalence L*≃Hom_Z(L,Z).
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: Dual/Basic.lean:123, noncomputable def dualPairingEquiv (L) [L.IsNondegenerate] : L.dualCarrier ≃ₗ[ℤ] Module.Dual ℤ L, with dualPairingEquiv_cast giving that it is the ambient form. Matches.

items.name: Discriminant group representative equality
items.statement: For an integral lattice L and x,y∈L*, [x]=[y] in L*/L iff x−y∈L; in particular [x]=0 iff x∈L.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: Discriminant/Group.lean:114 discriminantGroup_mk_eq_zero_iff and :121 discriminantGroup_mk_eq_iff (no nondegeneracy needed). Match.

items.name: Finiteness of the discriminant group
items.statement: The quotient L*/L of an integral lattice is finite iff its rational form is nondegenerate.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: Discriminant/Group.lean:133, Finite L.DiscriminantGroup ↔ L.form.Nondegenerate. Matches.

items.name: Half-norm discriminant quadratic map
items.statement: For an even integral lattice L, the discriminant quadratic map on [x] equals B(x,x)/2 mod Z. Its value vanishes iff B(x,x) is twice an integer.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: Discriminant/Quadratic.lean:129 discriminantQuadraticMap_mk (value L.form x x/2 in AddCircle 1) and :138 …_eq_zero_iff (∃ n, L.form x x = 2n); needs only IsEven. Matches. The paper's q: A_S→Q/2Z is twice this map.

items.name: Polarization of the discriminant quadratic map
items.statement: For an even integral lattice, q(x+y)−q(x)−q(y) is the discriminant bilinear pairing of x,y.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: Discriminant/Quadratic.lean:158, polar (discriminantQuadraticMap) x y = discriminantPairing x y. Matches.

items.name: Even overlattice correspondence
items.statement: For an even nondegenerate integral lattice L, the even intermediate carriers L⊂M⊂L* are order-isomorphic, via M↦M/L, to the quadratic-isotropic subgroups of its discriminant quadratic module.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Missing hypothesis: the declaration is in the scope of `variable [L.IsNondegenerate]` (Overlattice/Isotropic.lean:291; the def is at :343) and uses L.discriminantQuadraticModule, which is defined only for nondegenerate L. Review note: Library status is right (TauCeti.IntegralLattice.evenIntermediateCarrierOrderIsoIsotropicSubgroup at f790474). The lattices S of (14) and (16) are nondegenerate (det −4), so the application is unaffected.

items.name: Overlattice index equals subgroup order
items.statement: For an integral lattice L and intermediate carrier M, [M:L] equals the cardinality of its associated subgroup in L*/L.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: Overlattice/Index.lean:207, IntermediateCarrier.index_eq_natCard_discriminantSubgroup (M), with no nondegeneracy hypothesis. Matches.

items.name: Signed determinant and index square
items.statement: For an integral intermediate carrier M which is a full lattice, det(M)[M:L]²=det(L).
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: Overlattice/Index.lean:263, IsIntegral.determinant_mul_index_sq under [M.1.IsLattice ℚ]: determinant(M)·index²=determinant(L) in ℤ. Matches.

items.name: Discriminant and index square
items.statement: For an integral full intermediate lattice M, disc(M)[M:L]²=disc(L), using nonnegative discriminants.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: Overlattice/Index.lean:272, IsIntegral.discriminant_mul_index_sq (ℕ-valued discriminants). Matches.

items.name: Even D_n discriminant quadratic module
items.statement: For a positive even n, the positive-definite checkerboard D_n lattice has discriminant module (Z/2)² with vector half-norm 1/2, spinor and cospinor half-norm n/8, and vector-spinor pairing 1/2 mod Z.
items.locator: §§9, 12; TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/RootLattice/TypeD/Basic.lean, lines 1010–1110 (the standard (Z/2)² model checkerboardStandardQuadraticModule at :1018, the isometry at :1087)
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: checkerboardDiscriminantQuadraticIsometry (hn : Even n) with [NeZero n] identifies the discriminant module of checkerboardLattice n with the Klein-four model (vector 1/2, spinor and cospinor n/8, pairing 1/2). Matches. For D₈(−1) in (16) this gives vector 1/2 and spinors 0 mod Z, as the paper uses.

items.name: E₈ is even unimodular
items.statement: The standard positive E₈ root lattice is even and unimodular, with determinant 1.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: RootLattice/TypeE.lean:712 isEven_typeE₈RootLattice, :718 determinant = 1, :729 isUnimodular. Match.

items.name: E₈ as the D₈-plus lattice
items.statement: The standard E₈ root lattice is isometric to the even index-two spinor extension D₈⁺.
items.note: Actual statement read at Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369; only the abstract lattice contract is built, not its geometric realization. Review note: Read at f790474: RootLattice/D8Plus/Isometry.lean:296, typeE₈IsometryD8Plus : Isometry typeE₈RootLattice d8PlusLattice. Matches.

items.name: Surface Riemann–Roch
items.statement: For a smooth projective surface S over a field and divisor D, χ(O_S(D))=χ(O_S)+(D·(D−K_S))/2.
items.locator: §4, p. 12 ('must be even by Riemann–Roch'). The Riemann–Roch uses on p. 17 (proof of Theorem 5.6) and on p. 42 (proof of Proposition 12.2: 'By Riemann–Roch we have N_K(R)≃O_{Y_K}(R̃)') are Riemann–Roch on a genus-one CURVE, not the surface theorem (new coverage item).
items.note: Reviewed SF.5 audit and full source contract read; the surface theorem is planned, not inferred from existing abstract quadratic forms. Review note: Planned status right: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 names surface Riemann–Roch.

items.name: Adjunction on a smooth surface
items.statement: For an integral Cartier curve C on a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field, 2p_a(C)−2=C·(C+K_S).
items.locator: §§4, 6, 12; use over an algebraically closed field for the displayed numerical formula
items.note: Reviewed SF.5 audit and full source contract read; the surface theorem is planned, not inferred from existing abstract quadratic forms. Review note: Planned in SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 (adjunction is named there). Used in §12 to turn R̃²=−2 into R̃≅P¹ and R̃²=0 into a genus-one curve (K_Y≡0).

items.name: Hodge index for a surface
items.statement: For a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field and ample divisor H, the intersection form is negative definite on the H-orthogonal subspace of NS(S)⊗R.
items.note: Reviewed SF.5 audit and full source contract read; the surface theorem is planned, not inferred from existing abstract quadratic forms. Review note: Planned in SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 (Hodge index for smooth projective surfaces). In §§11–15 it is used also for 'distinct genus-one fibrations have F·F′≥1' (new coverage item).

items.name: Multiplicity and indecomposable fiber
items.statement: For a connected fiber-type effective divisor C=Σm_iC_i, its multiplicity is gcd_i m_i; C is simple if this is 1, multiple otherwise, and C_ind=Σ(m_i/m)C_i. Its reduction is ΣC_i, a different operation.

tests.name: MultiplicityandindecomposablefiberTest1
tests.statement: An I₄* fiber can be simple although some component coefficients are 2.

tests.name: MultiplicityandindecomposablefiberTest2
tests.statement: Multiplying a fiber divisor by 2 doubles its multiplicity.

tests.name: MultiplicityandindecomposablefiberTest3
tests.statement: A simple nonreduced fiber need not equal its reduction.

items.name: Semistable and unstable Kodaira symbols
items.statement: For a relatively minimal genus-one fibration, classify the underlying indecomposable geometric fiber: I_m with m≥1 is semistable/multiplicative; I_n* (n≥0),II,III,IV,IV*,III*,II* are unstable/additive; I₀ means a smooth elliptic underlying fiber.

tests.name: SemistableandunstableKodairasymbolsTest1
tests.statement: I₁ is semistable although its curve is irreducible.

tests.name: SemistableandunstableKodairasymbolsTest2
tests.statement: A smooth supersingular I₀ fiber is not additive.

tests.name: SemistableandunstableKodairasymbolsTest3
tests.statement: I₀* and I₀ have different component counts and reduction type.

items.name: Degenerate genus-one fiber
items.statement: A geometric fiber is degenerate when its underlying indecomposable curve is singular for an elliptic fibration, reducible for a quasielliptic fibration, or the fiber is multiple.

tests.name: DegenerategenusonefiberTest1
tests.statement: A multiple smooth elliptic fiber is degenerate.

tests.name: DegenerategenusonefiberTest2
tests.statement: A simple irreducible cuspidal fiber is the general quasielliptic fiber and is not degenerate in this convention.

tests.name: DegenerategenusonefiberTest3
tests.statement: Testing only geometric singularity misclassifies general quasielliptic fibers.

items.name: Nonsplit nodal conductor gluing
items.statement: Over a perfect field k, a rational nodal curve with nonsplit node is obtained by pinching Spec E⊂P¹_k, for a separable quadratic extension E/k, to Spec k; this is the symbol nonsplit I₁.

tests.name: NonsplitnodalconductorgluingTest1
tests.statement: Over F_q the count is q+2.

tests.name: NonsplitnodalconductorgluingTest2
tests.statement: Split I₁ instead identifies two rational points and has q points.

tests.name: NonsplitnodalconductorgluingTest3
tests.statement: A nonsplit node is not a cusp: its conductor algebra is a field, not k[ε]/ε².

items.name: Nonsplit two-component conductor gluing
items.statement: Over a perfect field k, nonsplit I₂ is the curve with normalization P¹⊔P¹ obtained from the conductor square Spec(E×E)→P¹⊔P¹ and Spec E→C, where E/k is separable quadratic.

tests.name: NonsplittwocomponentconductorgluingTest1
tests.statement: Over F_q it has 2q+2 points.

tests.name: NonsplittwocomponentconductorgluingTest2
tests.statement: Its two components are defined over k although their intersection points need not be.

tests.name: NonsplittwocomponentconductorgluingTest3
tests.statement: A split component graph does not force the two nodes to be k-rational.

items.name: Strong p-adic Hensel lemma
items.statement: Let p be prime, R a commutative semiring with an algebra map to Z_p, F∈R[X], and a∈Z_p. If ||F(a)||<||F′(a)||², there is a root z with ||z−a||<||F′(a)|| and ||F′(z)||=||F′(a)||, unique among roots satisfying that strict distance bound.
items.note: Actual generic coefficient hypotheses and full conclusion read at the pinned Mathlib commit. This does not by itself construct geometric sections of an algebraic space. Review note: Library status confirmed: mathlib:hensels_lemma at 082e2d3, Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Hensel.lean:461, with [CommSemiring R] [Algebra R ℤ_[p]], F : Polynomial R, hypothesis ‖F.aeval a‖ < ‖F.derivative.aeval a‖², and exactly the stated conclusion.

items.name: Dyadic unit square criterion
items.statement: For u∈Z₂×, u is a square in Q₂ iff u≡1 mod 8.
items.locator: Conrad Hensel’s Lemma, Theorem 4.5 and proof, p. 7; supplementary input to Proposition 5.5 repair
items.note: The layer explicitly plans U(Q₂,3)⊂squares and the sharpness witness 5. Necessity is reduction of an odd square modulo 8. Reviewed AUDIT-04 says the dyadic result is absent; do not cite the prime-to-residue-characteristic power-subgroup API at p=2. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Necessity: odd squares are 1 mod 8 (checked mod 2^k for k=3..12). Sufficiency: apply hensels_lemma to X²−u at a=1, where |F(1)|=|1−u|≤1/8<1/4=|F′(1)|². Planned status acceptable. LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1 plans unitFiltration_le_range_powMonoidHom_two, U(K,2e+1)⊆(K^×)², which for Q₂ is 1+8Z₂, together with the sharpness at depth 2e. The converse direction is not stated there and belongs in this node.

items.name: Eight dyadic square classes in normal form
items.statement: Every c∈Q₂^× is congruent modulo (Q₂^×)² to exactly one element (−1)^e2^a5^b with e,a,b∈{0,1}; equivalently Q₂^×/(Q₂^×)² is elementary abelian of order 8 with basis the classes of −1, 2, 5.
items.locator: Conrad Theorems 3.2, 4.5; elementary deduction in this continuation’s cover-comparison proof
items.note: Application of the existing layer’s multiplicative-group, dyadic eight-class and deep-unit contracts: valuation parity and odd residue modulo 8 give the explicit basis. This basis computation is an application, not a second local-field roadmap. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Wording: every element trivially has a unique square class. What is unique is the representative triple. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Write c=2^v u with u∈Z₂^×. Then a≡v mod 2, and u mod 8∈{1,5,7,3} corresponds to (e,b)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1), using −1≡7 and −5≡3 mod 8. Uniqueness holds because the eight representatives have distinct pairs (v mod 2, u mod 8), and by /173 these pairs are square-class invariants. Planned: Layer 1 plans the count 8 (card_squareClasses_dyadic); the basis is an application.

items.name: Unramified quadratic correction torsor
items.statement: The Z₂-algebra B=Z₂[z]/(z²−z−1), with involution z↦1−z, defines a finite étale Z/2-torsor. Its generic fiber is Q₂(√5), and its special fiber is F₄.
items.locator: Supplementary dyadic model in the Proposition 5.5 repair; LocalFieldsRamification Layer 2 worked Q₂(√5) example
items.note: Discriminant 5 is a unit; modulo 2 the polynomial is irreducible and separable. The involution exchanges its roots. This gives an actual integral model; Z₂[s]/(s²−5) is not an étale model. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Discriminant of z²−z−1 is 5∈Z₂^×. Modulo 2, f(0)=f(1)=1, so the residue algebra is F₄. (2z−1)²=4z²−4z+1≡5 mod f, and f(1−z)=f(z). Since (z−σz)²=5 is a unit, B⊗B→B×B, x⊗y↦(xy,xσy), is an isomorphism, so B is a Z/2-torsor. With s=2z−1 we get σs=−s, so the generic fibre is the Kummer torsor Q₂[s]/(s²−5) of class 5. The class becomes trivial over W(F̄₂). Planned via Layer 2's worked Q₂(√5) example: acceptable.
api: finite-étale torsor identity and residue extension

items.name: Canonical-cover twists supported at two
items.statement: Let S=Spec Z[1/2], Y/S an Enriques family with Pic^τ=μ₂, and X→Y a canonical Z/2-cover. For u∈{1,−1,2,−2}, the contracted product X^(u)=(X×_S Spec O_S[s]/(s²−u))/(Z/2) is a canonical finite étale double cover of Y.
items.locator: Proposition 5.4 twisting action; explicit construction supplementing Proposition 5.5
api: compatibility with pullback and composition of twists
preservation of the edge-map canonical-cover class

tests.statement: u=1 yields the original cover up to isomorphism.

items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Over Z[1/2], O_S[s]/(s²−u) with s↦−s is a finite étale Z/2-torsor for u∈{±1,±2}: 2 and u are units, so s²−u is separable. These four are all of H¹(Z[1/2],Z/2)=Z[1/2]^×/squares, because Pic(Z[1/2])=0. The contracted product has class [X]+f*[T_u]. It maps to the same section of R¹f_*G, so it is again canonical. u=1 gives the split torsor, since (s−1) and (s+1) are comaximal when 2 is invertible.

items.name: Canonical cover over Z₂ before Picard constancy
items.statement: If Y/Z is an Enriques family with Pic^τ=μ₂, its restriction to Z₂ has a canonical finite étale double cover X₂→Y_Z₂.
items.locator: Proposition 5.5 repair, step 1; Corollary 7.3 and Proposition 5.4(ii)
items.note: Minkowski first makes Num constant. Corollary 7.3 uses Num only and gives 25 points on Y_F₂. Smooth henselian lifting gives Y(Z₂)≠∅, so Proposition 5.4(ii) applies. Neither full Picard constancy nor Theorem 15.1 is used. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Chain: π₁(Spec Z)=1 gives constant Num (/181). Corollary 7.3 (/80) then gives #Y(F₂)=25, which needs only constant Num, b₁=0 and b₂=ρ=10, so the argument is not circular. /185 lifts a point to Y(Z₂), and Proposition 5.4(ii) gives X₂. Here G=P^D=Z/2 is constant over Z, so X₂ is finite étale. Remark: the section is not even needed here, because H²_fppf(Z₂,Z/2)=H²_ét(Z₂,Z/2)=H²(F₂,Z/2)=0. The Z_p-sections are needed anyway for /184.

items.name: Dyadic difference class of canonical covers
items.statement: For two canonical Z/2-covers of the same Enriques surface over Q₂, their difference under the twisting action is a class in H¹(Q₂,Z/2)=Q₂×/Q₂×². In particular this applies to a cover over Z[1/2] and the generic fiber of the cover in /177.
items.locator: Proposition 5.4 final assertion; repair of Proposition 5.5
items.note: Identify Z/2 with μ₂ only over Q₂, where 2 is invertible. Kummer over Z₂ classifies μ₂-torsors, not all finite étale Z/2-torsors. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Both Q₂-restrictions map to the base change of [𝔛], which is compatible with base change because it is defined by P⊂Pic. By sequence (2) over Spec Q₂, canonical covers form a principal homogeneous space under H¹(Q₂,G). Z/2≅μ₂ over Q₂, and Kummer theory gives Q₂^×/Q₂^{×2}.

items.name: Removing the ramified part of the difference
items.statement: Let c∈Q₂×/Q₂×² be a difference class as in /178. Exactly one u∈{1,−1,2,−2} has cu∈{1,5}. Twisting the global cover by u and the Z₂-cover by the trivial torsor or /175, respectively, makes their Q₂-fibers isomorphic.
items.locator: This continuation’s proof of the previously unverified Proposition 5.5 comparison
items.note: If c=(−1)^e2^a5^b, choose u=(−1)^e2^a. Each class has exponent 2, so cu=5^b. The remaining class already has a finite étale Z₂-model; no approximation over Frac W(F₂bar) is asserted. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Exhaustively checked for all eight classes: exactly one u∈{1,−1,2,−2} has cu∈{1,5}, namely u=(−1)^e2^a. Twisting the global cover by u changes the difference to cu=5^b. Twisting X₂ by B^b then makes the difference trivial, so the two Q₂-fibres are isomorphic as G-torsors over Y_{Q₂}.

items.name: Everywhere unramified number fields have degree one
items.statement: For a number field F, if each nonzero prime ideal q of its ring of integers has ramification index 1 over Z, then [F:Q]=1.
items.locator: TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Inertia.lean:89; arithmetic input used on main-paper p. 15
items.note: Actual statement and hypotheses read at f790474. The scheme-theoretic finite-étale translation remains a separate item /181. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Library status confirmed: tauceti:NumberField.finrank_eq_one_of_forall_ramificationIdx_eq_one at f790474, TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Inertia.lean:89. Hypothesis: every nonzero prime ideal of 𝓞 F has ramificationIdx over ℤ equal to 1. Conclusion: Module.finrank ℚ F = 1. It is proved from Mathlib's NumberField.exists_not_isUnramifiedIn.

items.name: The étale fundamental group of Spec Z is trivial
items.statement: Every connected nonempty finite étale cover of Spec Z is isomorphic to Spec Z; consequently π₁(Spec Z)=1 and every finite-rank locally constant free abelian sheaf on Spec Z is constant.
items.locator: Proposition 5.5 first paragraph; deduction from /180 and the finite-étale Galois category
items.note: A connected finite étale Z-algebra is a normal domain, hence the full ring of integers of its fraction number field; its ramification indices are 1. Import /180. This is not already the statement of the number-field declaration. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound, with one step to add. The finite-étale part is right: a connected finite étale Z-algebra is a normal domain, hence the maximal order of its fraction field, unramified everywhere, hence Z by /180. The 'consequently' for local systems with infinite stalks needs more: Num has stalk Z^10, and its monodromy group O(U⊕E₈) is infinite. The missing step uses the normality of Spec Z. A connected component T₀ of the étale Isom(Z^10_S,Num)-torsor is normal and connected, hence integral, so its generic fibre is a single point Spec L with L/Q finite. Its stabilizer H⊂GL₁₀(Z) therefore acts simply transitively on the [L:Q] geometric generic points, so H is finite, and T₀ is a finite étale H-torsor, trivial by the first part. The paper uses the same fact silently ('comes from a representation of π₁'). State it in the node.

items.name: Picard classes are represented when a section exists
items.statement: Let f:X→B be a morphism of algebraic spaces with a section σ and universally O_T≅f_{T,*}O_{X_T}. For every B-scheme T, the sequence 0→Pic(T)→Pic(X_T)→Pic_{X/B}(T)→0 is split exact, with retraction σ_T*.
items.locator: Stacks Lemma 99.11.4, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D24; local-projectivity supplement to Proposition 5.5
items.note: Statement and descent proof read. The section rigidifies descent isomorphisms; no vanishing of Br(B) is needed. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Statement matches Stacks Lemma 99.11.4 (tag 0D24; read in 0D24.html), in Situation 99.11.1. The hypothesis that O_T→f_{T,*}O_{X_T} is an isomorphism for all T holds for Enriques families: they are flat, proper and finitely presented with geometrically connected, geometrically reduced fibres.

items.name: Lifting twice a numerical class
items.statement: For an exact sequence 0→P→Q→N→0 of abelian fppf sheaves with 2P=0, multiplication by 2 on Q descends uniquely to a map d:N→Q, with projection∘d=[2]_N. Apply this to Pic^τ→Pic→Num of an Enriques family in the Pic^τ=μ₂ branch.
items.locator: Elementary sheaf descent supplement to Proposition 5.5, using its exact sequence(3)
api: unique factorization through the sheaf quotient

tests.name: SCH23_183_1
tests.statement: For a split extension P⊕N, d(n)=(0,2n).

tests.statement: Two local lifts differ by P and therefore have the same double.
