items.name: Local projectivity for the excluded μ₂ branch
items.statement: Let R be a noetherian local ring and Y/R an Enriques family with a section, constant Num, and Pic^τ annihilated by 2. Then Y is a projective R-scheme. In particular an Enriques family over Z in the Pic^τ=μ₂ branch becomes projective over Z_p for every prime p.
items.locator: This continuation’s local-model supplement to Proposition 5.5
items.note: Lift the numerical class of an ample line bundle on the closed fiber to constant Num(R); /183 and /182 give a line bundle with twice that numerical class. Ampleness on the projective closed surface is invariant under numerical equivalence. /186 spreads ampleness over the local base, so Y is a scheme and projective. For R=Z_p, /79 gives 1+10p+p² rational points; /185 supplies the section. No claim that an arbitrary proper algebraic space is projective. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound; the projectivity claim is true. Proof: take an ample H̄ on the geometric closed fibre Ȳ₀. Constant Num gives n∈Num_{𝔜/R}(R) restricting to [H̄]. /183 gives d(n)∈Pic_{𝔜/R}(R), and the section with /182 gives L∈Pic(𝔜) representing d(n). Then L|Ȳ₀≡H̄^{⊗2} numerically, so L|Ȳ₀ is ample by Nakai–Moishezon. /186 then gives an open V⊂Spec R containing the closed point, so V=Spec R. Hence 𝔜 is representable, that is a scheme, and L is relatively ample. Proper with an f-ample sheaf over a noetherian affine base gives a closed immersion into P^N_R, so 𝔜 is projective. Precision to add: /186 as stated (0D3A) needs the closed fibre 𝔜⊗k to be a scheme with L ample on it, while the note argues on 'the projective closed surface'. Either apply the general form 0D3D to Spec k̄→Spec R, whose geometric fibre is a scheme with L ample, or first show that 𝔜⊗k is a scheme. The hypothesis 'Pic^τ killed by 2' is automatic (see /183). For R=Z_p the section comes from /80 (1+10p+p²>0 points) and /185. The claim does not use the μ₂ hypothesis.

items.name: Smooth henselian lifting for the local family
items.statement: Let R be a henselian local ring with residue field k, and X/R a smooth separated algebraic space. Every k-point lifts to an R-point.
items.locator: Stacks Lemma 68.11.4 at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EMV and Lemma 15.13.3 at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H74
items.note: A separated space is decent. Choose an affine étale neighborhood with the same residue field at the given point, then apply smooth-algebra lifting for (R,m). Statements and proofs read; this avoids presuming X was a scheme. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Separated implies decent. Stacks Lemma 68.11.4 (tag 0EMV) gives an affine étale (U,u)→(X,x) with κ(u)=κ(x)=k, so the k-point factors through U. Stacks Lemma 15.13.3 (tag 0H74), applied to the henselian pair (R,m) and the smooth R-algebra O(U), lifts it to an R-point.

items.name: Spreading a fiberwise ample line bundle
items.statement: Let f:X→B be a proper algebraic space over a noetherian scheme and L an invertible sheaf. If X_b is a scheme and L_b is ample, some open neighborhood V of b makes X_V a scheme with L_V relatively ample.
items.note: Import the existing relative-ampleness and algebraic-space-descent owners. Read the proof constructing a finite morphism to projective space; ampleness is an essential hypothesis, not a consequence of properness alone. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The statement matches Stacks Lemma 71.15.3 (tag 0D3A). The proof of 0D3A shows that X_V is a scheme: after shrinking, the morphism to P^r_V is finite. Status: 'planned' is doubtful. R09.1 plans relative ampleness and very ampleness for schemes, and R09.3 plans algebraic-space quotients and descent. Neither names openness of ampleness for proper algebraic spaces with the representability conclusion (0D3A, or the general 0D3D, which /184 actually needs). Either add it explicitly to R09.3 or A0-extension, or mark the item missing with a source route there. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): status changed from planned (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1, AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.3) to missing: R09.1 plans relative ampleness for schemes and R09.3 algebraic-space quotients, but neither names openness of ampleness for proper algebraic spaces with the representability conclusion (Stacks 0D3A, or 0D3D, which /184 needs). Routed to NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent with the other representability inputs of the Proposition 5.5 repair.

items.name: Finite étale twisting preserves good models
items.statement: Let R be a ring, Y/R smooth proper, G/R finite étale, X→Y a finite étale G-torsor, and T/R a G-torsor, with G commutative. The contracted product X×^G T remains finite étale over Y and smooth proper over R. If Y is projective over R, the contracted product is a projective R-scheme.
items.locator: Effective descent applied to Proposition 5.4 twists; finite étale descent and pullback of an ample line bundle
items.note: Descend the finite étale morphism to Y, then pull back Y’s ample line bundle. This is not a claim that arbitrary unpolarized projective varieties descend as projective schemes. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. X×^G T=(X×_R T)/G is a G_Y-torsor for commutative G, of class [X]+f*[T], by descent. Being finite étale over Y, it is smooth and proper over R. It is finite over Y, so it is a scheme when Y is, and the pullback of an ample sheaf along a finite morphism is ample. Planned via SF.1 and R09.3: acceptable.

items.name: Étale canonical covers are K3 surfaces
items.statement: For an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field whose canonical-cover Cartier dual G is étale of rank 2, its canonical G-torsor is a smooth connected K3 surface. This includes ordinary Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2 and all Enriques surfaces in characteristic different from 2.
items.locator: Main-paper §4 and Proposition 5.5; canonical-cover theorem from the Enriques prerequisites
items.note: Distinct from /40–/41, which concern the singular K3-like covers in the simply connected characteristic-two cases. The geometric K3 theorem is imported; the original Enriques prerequisite proof remains in the recursive-source gap. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. G étale of rank 2 means P≅μ₂ with G=Z/2 (ordinary, characteristic 2) or P≅Z/2≅μ₂ (characteristic ≠2). The torsor is nontrivial because it corresponds to the inclusion P⊂Pic, and is therefore connected. It is étale, so X is smooth. ω_X=ε*ω_Y is trivial, since ω_Y is O_Y or is the 2-torsion class that defines the cover. χ(O_X)=2χ(O_Y)=2 with h⁰=h²=1 gives h¹(O_X)=0.

items.name: Kodaira–Néron classification of fibers of genus-one fibrations
items.statement: Let f:S→B be a relatively minimal genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface over an algebraically closed field. For every closed point b the underlying indecomposable curve of canonical type f⁻¹_ind(b)=Σn_iC_i is one of: I₀ (a smooth genus-one curve); I₁ (a rational nodal curve); I_m, m≥2 (a cycle of m smooth rational (−2)-curves, all n_i=1); II (a rational cuspidal curve); III (two smooth rational curves meeting in one point with multiplicity 2); IV (three smooth rational curves through one point); I_n*, n≥0 (n+5 components, dual graph the extended Dynkin diagram D̃_{n+4}); IV*, III*, II* (7, 8, 9 components, dual graphs Ẽ₆, Ẽ₇, Ẽ₈), the n_i being the coefficients of the null root. The components of a reducible fiber are (−2)-curves, and its intersection matrix is negative semidefinite with radical generated by f⁻¹_ind(b).
items.note: Néron 1964 and Kodaira 1963; valid in every characteristic, and for quasi-elliptic fibrations (characteristic 2 and 3) the reducible fibers are of additive type. Items /167–/171 define the symbols and their twisted forms; this is the classification theorem they presuppose. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 plans the equation-level Kodaira types over a DVR, not fibers of fibered surfaces. Review note: missing is right. The radical assertion (Zariski's lemma) is needed more generally in Theorem 2.1: for any contraction onto a curve, over a non-closed field. It is proposed as a separate item under coverage.

items.name: Kodaira symbols for schematic fibers over non-closed fields (Szydło)
items.statement: Let f: S → B be a relatively minimal genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface over a field k with h⁰(O_S) = 1, and a ∈ B a closed point. Suppose every irreducible component of S_a is birational to P¹_{κ(a)}. Then Γ(S_ā) → Γ(S_a) is a graph isomorphism. It respects edge labels when the label of an edge of Γ(S_a) is dim_{κ(a)} H⁰(O_{D_i ∩ D_j}) = (D_i·D_j)/[κ(a):k]; this equals (D_i·D_j) when κ(a) = k. The Kodaira symbols of (1) then designate f⁻¹_ind(a), with one exception for r ≤ 2 components. There the conductor-square description (Spec R → P¹, resp. Spec(R × R) → P¹ ⊔ P¹, with R of length two over κ(a)) also allows R a field, giving the twisted symbols Ĩ₁, ĨI (r = 1) and Ĩ₂, ĨII (r = 2). Over a perfect residue field only Ĩ₁ and Ĩ₂ occur.
items.note: Szydło, Elliptic fibers over non-perfect residue fields, J. Number Theory 104 (2004), 75–99; stated as the paper uses it. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: With /9's labels (intersection numbers on S over k), 'respecting edge labels' fails when κ(a) ≠ k: components birational to P¹_{κ(a)} give (D_i·D_j) = [κ(a):k]·(C_i·C_j). Labels must be measured over κ(a), or 'birational to P¹' read over k, which forces κ(a) = k. The paper's reading is over k, since its proof of (iii)⇒(ii) in Proposition 3.1 is 'trivial'. Also /170–/171 define only Ĩ₁ and Ĩ₂ over perfect fields, so they do not supply ĨI and ĨII.

items.name: Canonical bundle formula for genus-one fibrations (Bombieri–Mumford)
items.statement: Let f:S→B be a relatively minimal genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface over an algebraically closed field, with multiple fibers m_iF_i. Write R¹f_*O_S=L⊕T with L invertible and T torsion. Then ω_S≅f*(ω_B⊗L^{−1})⊗O_S(Σa_iF_i) with 0≤a_i≤m_i−1, a_i=m_i−1 for every tame multiple fiber, and deg L^{−1}=χ(O_S)+length(T).
items.note: Bombieri–Mumford, Enriques' classification of surfaces in char. p, II (1977), Theorem 2. Used for ω_J=φ*O(d) in /72 and for ω_Y≅O_Y(F₁−F₂) in /35.

items.name: Tame and wild multiple fibers
items.statement: Let f:S→B be a relatively minimal genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface over an algebraically closed field, and mF (m≥2, F the underlying indecomposable curve) a multiple fibre over b. Then O_F(F) has finite order ν dividing m. The fibre is tame if ν=m and wild otherwise, and it is wild exactly when b lies in the support of the torsion of R¹f_*O_S. On an Enriques surface with H¹(Y,O_Y)=0 the torsion of R¹φ_*O_Y vanishes, so every multiple fibre is tame, and each double fibre 2F has O_F(F) of order 2 in Pic(F).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 4.3, p. 12; proof of Theorem 5.6(iv), pp. 17–18
items.note: Raynaud; Bombieri–Mumford II, §2; Katsura–Ueno. Lemma 4.3 (/36) and Theorem 5.6(iv) (/69) consume it. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Minor: the tame/wild theory (Bombieri–Mumford II, Katsura–Ueno) is for a relatively minimal genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface; add these hypotheses. The Theorem 5.6(iv) use is on p. 18.

items.name: Lang's theorem for genus-one curves over finite fields
items.statement: Every torsor under a connected algebraic group over a finite field is trivial (Lang 1956, Theorem 2). In particular every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus one over F_q has an F_q-point and is an elliptic curve.
items.locator: §3 before Proposition 3.3, p. 11; proof of Proposition 9.2, p. 24
items.note: Not planned in the atlas: no layer treats Galois cohomology of connected algebraic groups over finite fields. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3 counts points of elliptic curves, not of torsors. Review note: missing confirmed. No atlas stage plans Lang's theorem on torsors under connected groups over finite fields.

items.name: Twisted forms of P¹ over finite fields
items.statement: A proper curve C over F_q with C⊗F̄_q≅P¹ is isomorphic to P¹_{F_q}, because Br(F_q)=0 by Wedderburn's little theorem. Over any field, a twisted form of P¹ that carries a line bundle of degree one is isomorphic to P¹.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 3.1, p. 11; proof of Theorem 5.6(iii), p. 17
items.note: Mathlib has Wedderburn's little theorem (Mathlib/RingTheory/LittleWedderburn.lean:166, littleWedderburn); Brauer–Severi curves and the Brauer group of a field are not in the libraries at the pins. Review note: Partly library, and the note is wrong to say the Brauer group of a field is absent at the pins. Br(F_q) = 0 is tauceti:TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite (TauCeti/Algebra/BrauerGroup/Trivial.lean:247 at f790474), for Mathlib's BrauerGroup (Mathlib/Algebra/BrauerGroup/Defs.lean:99). The second sentence is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-5-consequences-of-riemannroch-and-local-components (Stichtenoth Prop. 1.6.3: genus 0 with a divisor of degree one ⟺ rational). Still missing: the Brauer–Severi link from twisted forms of P¹ to central simple algebras. Over F_q a shorter route avoids it: the anticanonical embedding makes C a plane conic, mathlib:char_dvd_card_solutions (Mathlib/FieldTheory/ChevalleyWarning.lean:178) gives it an F_q-point, and Layer 5 then gives C ≅ P¹.

items.name: Isogenous elliptic curves over a finite field have the same point counts
items.statement: If elliptic curves E and E′ over F_q are isogenous over F_q, then #E(F_{q^r})=#E′(F_{q^r}) for every r≥1. This is the direction of Tate's isogeny theorem (Tate 1966, Theorem 1) that the paper uses.
items.note: Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layers 1 and 3 plan isogenies commuting with Frobenius and #E(F_q)=deg(1−π_q); the invariance of the counts under isogeny is not stated there. FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4 plans the isogeny theorem over number fields.

items.name: Invariants of rational elliptic surfaces
items.statement: Let φ:J→P¹ be a relatively minimal elliptic fibration with a section E of a smooth projective rational surface over an algebraically closed field. Then ω_J≅φ*O_{P¹}(−1), K_J²=0 and (E·E)=−1, and J is obtained from P² by nine blowing-ups; hence b₂(J)=ρ(J)=10 and Num(J) is odd unimodular of signature (1,9).
items.locator: proof of Proposition 6.1, p. 18; proof of Corollary 7.3, p. 21; proof of Proposition 9.5, p. 27
items.note: Cossec–Dolgachev 1989, Proposition 5.6.1. /72 records the consequences for the Weierstrass model.

items.name: Quasi-elliptic fibrations in characteristic two
items.statement: Quasi-elliptic fibrations exist only in characteristics 2 and 3. For a quasi-elliptic fibration φ:S→P¹ of a smooth projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2, every fiber is irreducible cuspidal (type II) or reducible of type III, I*_{2n}, III* or II* (with 2, 2n+5, 8 and 9 components), and the Mordell–Weil group of the jacobian is killed by 2. Hence ρ(S)=2+Σ_b(r_b−1), r_b the number of components of the fiber over b; for ρ(S)=10 this gives Σ_b(r_b−1)=8.
items.note: Cossec–Dolgachev 1989, Theorems 5.7.4–5.7.6. /120 and /121 consume it. Review note: Statement is as the paper uses it (p. 33); the component counts and the Shioda–Tate consequence are correct (Pic⁰(Y_K) has the rank of J(K), which is finite). The Cossec–Dolgachev theorem numbers 5.7.4–5.7.6 were not checked (book not available).

items.name: Lang's classification of rational elliptic surfaces in characteristic two (as used)
items.statement: (Lang 2000) Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2 the configurations of singular fibers of relatively minimal rational jacobian elliptic surfaces are classified, with normal forms of their Weierstrass equations y²+a₁xy+a₃y=x³+a₂x²+a₄x+a₆ (deg a_i≤i). The paper uses: (a) if the functional j-invariant is non-zero there is exactly one additive fiber; (b) II+I₉ does not occur; (c) a III fiber occurs together with a semistable fiber I_m, 6≤m≤9, only as III+I₆ and III+I₈; (d) II* and I₃* whose two other rational fibers are smooth force exactly one further singular fiber, of type I₁, and so does IV*+E+I₃; (e) with j≠0, III* occurs only in Lang's Case 7, with singular fibers III*+I₁+I₁; (f) with j=0 there are at most three singular fibers, and a non-reduced fiber forces the remaining rational fiber to be smooth (Lang 2000, p. 5829); (g) the normal forms of Lang's Cases 2A, 5A, 5D, 7, 13A and 14 quoted in the proofs of Theorems 10.4 and 10.5.
items.note: W. Lang, Configurations of singular fibres on rational elliptic surfaces in characteristic two, Comm. Algebra 28 (2000), 5813–5836, is a prerequisite and was not re-derived. The finite checks for /104–/114 confirm the eleven equations (discriminants, j-invariants, smooth fibers), not the exhaustiveness in (a)–(g). Review note: The list of uses is incomplete. The proof of Theorem 10.4 also uses Lang to reduce r_a=6 to I₁*+E₄+I₄ (excluding I₁*+I₅), r_a=7 to IV*+E₄+I₃, r_a=8 to III*+E₄+I₂, r_a=9 to II*+E₄+I₁, and to exclude I₂* in Theorem 10.5. In the twisted case the paper's use of the classification misses three configurations (new issue). Over F₂ all of (a)–(g) can be replaced by the finite computation described at /115, so /198 need not be a dependency of Theorems 10.4 and 10.5. Part (f) also follows from Δ=a₃⁴ when a₁=0, as the referee remarks.

items.name: Additive reduction from c₄, and Tate's algorithm
items.statement: For a Weierstrass equation over a DVR with perfect residue field whose reduction is singular (Δ in the maximal ideal), the reduction is additive if and only if c₄ lies in the maximal ideal (Deligne, Formulaire, Proposition 5.1); in characteristic 2, c₄=a₁⁴. From a minimal Weierstrass equation, Tate's algorithm computes the Kodaira type, the number of components and the splitness of the special fiber of the minimal regular model.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 10.3, p. 29; proof of Theorem 10.4, pp. 30–31
items.note: Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 4 plans reduction types, Kodaira types and Tate's algorithm over a DVR. The singular-reduction hypothesis is needed: a smooth supersingular fiber in characteristic 2 also has c₄=0 (sourceIssue E15). Review note: Correct if 'the reduction' means the reduced cubic of the given equation, since cusp ⇔ c₄∈m. As a statement about the reduction type of the curve it needs a minimal equation. The paper applies it to the minimal global Weierstrass model, so this is fine.

items.name: Weierstrass curves, their invariants and changes of coordinates
items.statement: A Weierstrass curve over a commutative ring R is a tuple (a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄,a₆)∈R⁵, with invariants b₂,b₄,b₆,b₈,c₄,c₆, discriminant Δ, j-invariant j=c₄³/Δ when Δ is a unit, and the admissible changes of coordinates (u,r,s,t) acting on the coefficients.
items.note: Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Weierstrass.lean:77 (WeierstrassCurve), :121 (c₄), :132 (Δ), :389 (j, defined as Δ′⁻¹·c₄³ under IsElliptic); VariableChange.lean:57. Review note: Checked at Mathlib 082e2d3: Weierstrass.lean:77 (structure WeierstrassCurve), :121 (c₄), :132 (Δ), j as Δ′⁻¹·c₄³; VariableChange.lean:57 and the MulAction at :146.

items.name: Zeta functions and the Weil conjectures (as used)
items.statement: For X smooth proper over F_q, the zeta function Z(X,t)=exp(Σ_s N_s t^s/s) is rational (Dwork); the ℓ-adic cohomology H^i(X̄,Q_ℓ(j)) is finite-dimensional, with H^i(X̄,Q_ℓ(j))=H^i(X̄,Q_ℓ)⊗Q_ℓ(j); the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula gives Z(X,t)=∏_i det(1−t f_i)^{(−1)^{i+1}}, f_i the geometric Frobenius on H^i(X̄,Q_ℓ); Poincaré duality holds; and the eigenvalues of f_i are algebraic integers of absolute value q^{i/2} in every complex embedding (Deligne).
items.note: WeilConjectures WC.1 plans rationality and the point-count API, WC.2 Poincaré duality and WC.3 integrality and the Riemann hypothesis; the trace formula comes from the pinned point-counting source that WC.0 and EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.8 cite. Integrality holds for the untwisted f_i, not for all twists (sourceIssue E10).

items.name: Cycle class maps and base change
items.statement: For X smooth over a perfect field k there are cycle class maps CH^j(X)→H^{2j}(X,Q_ℓ(j)), compatible with base change to k̄ (the square (8)).
items.note: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.3 plans cycle classes over perfect fields, including finite fields. Review note: EDC.3 plans the cycle class map over perfect fields. It does not list compatibility with extension of the base field or flat pullback, which is what square (8) needs. Add it as an EDC.3 requirement.

items.name: Brauer–Hasse–Noether sequence for ℚ
items.statement: The sequence 0→Br(ℚ)→⊕_v Br(ℚ_v)→ℚ/ℤ→0, v running over all places including the real one, is exact.
items.note: Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 plans this sequence for number fields, with the real place. Review note: Planned status confirmed: TauCetiRoadmap ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 plans eq_zero_of_localInv_eq_zero (exactness at Br K), sumLocalInv_eq_zero, exists_br_of_sum_eq_zero, and the real Brauer group cyclic of order two.

items.name: Pic(ℤ)=0 and Br(ℤ)=0
items.statement: Pic(Spec ℤ)=0, since ℤ is a principal ideal domain, and Br(Spec ℤ)=0: Br(ℤ) injects into Br(ℚ) because Spec ℤ is regular of dimension one; its classes are unramified at every prime because Br(ℤ_p)=Br(F_p)=0; so by the Brauer–Hasse–Noether sequence (/203) such a class is determined by its real invariant, which the sum formula forces to vanish.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 5.5, pp. 15–16; Theorem 5.6 applied to R=ℤ
items.note: The étale Brauer group of a scheme and the injection Br(X)→Br(K) for regular integral X of dimension one are not planned; /203 supplies the field sequence. Review note: Statement and argument correct. Missing is right: ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 gives the field sequence only; Br of a scheme, Br(Z_p)≅Br(F_p) for the henselian Z_p, and injectivity of Br(Spec Z)→Br(Q) are not planned. Br(F_p)=0 can use Mathlib's littleWedderburn.

items.name: Kummer sequences over a base
items.statement: For S=Spec R, the fppf Kummer sequence 0→μ₂→G_m→G_m→0 (the second map squaring) gives exact sequences 0→R^×/R^{×2}→H¹_fppf(S,μ₂)→Pic(S)[2]→0 and Pic(S)→Pic(S)→H²_fppf(S,μ₂)→H²(S,G_m)→H²(S,G_m), the unlabelled maps being multiplication by 2. In particular Pic(S)=0 and H²(S,G_m)=0 (or only H²(S,G_m)[2]=0) give H¹(S,μ₂)=R^×/R^{×2} and H²(S,μ₂)=0.
items.note: SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 owns fppf and étale cohomology of schemes; this computation is not stated there. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): statement corrected against the paper: Pin 'Br(S)' as H²(S,G_m) (fppf = étale cohomology, by Grothendieck). The Kummer sequence gives exactness with H²(S,G_m), which is what the paper uses; with the Azumaya Brauer group one also needs Gabber's theorem for affine S. Review note: Missing confirmed: TauCetiRoadmap ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 plans the Kummer sequence only over fields with n invertible, not fppf over a base.

items.name: Tsen's theorem
items.statement: For an algebraically closed field k, the field k(t) is C₁, so Br(k(t))=0. Consequently, for a proper curve C over k(t) with H⁰(C,O_C)=k(t), every k(t)-point of Pic_{C/k(t)} comes from a line bundle on C.
items.note: The paper applies Tsen's theorem to F₂(t), where it fails (sourceIssue E13); the repair in /94 uses it over F̄₂(t) only.

items.name: Classification of indefinite unimodular lattices
items.statement: An indefinite unimodular lattice is determined up to isometry by its rank, signature and parity (Milnor–Husemoller, Chapter II, Theorem 5.3). In particular an even unimodular lattice of signature (1,9) is isometric to U⊕E₈(−1).
items.note: Tau Ceti has the hyperbolic plane, E₈ as D₈⁺ and unimodularity (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Examples.lean:81, hyperbolicPlane; RootLattice/D8Plus/Basic.lean:164, d8PlusLattice; Unimodular.lean:56, IsUnimodular) but not the classification of indefinite forms; Tau Ceti GlobalQuadraticForms classifies rational quadratic forms, not lattices. /29 consumes it. Review note: Missing confirmed at f790474: IntegralLattice has hyperbolicPlane (Examples.lean:81), the D₈⁺ model of E₈ and IsUnimodular, but no classification of indefinite unimodular forms (Milnor–Husemoller II.5.3, i.e. Serre's theorem).

items.name: Norm maps on Picard groups
items.statement: For a finite locally free morphism π:X′→X of constant rank n there is a norm homomorphism N:Pic(X′)→Pic(X), compatible with base change, with N(π*L)≅L^{⊗n} for every line bundle L on X (EGA II, §6.5).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 1.1, p. 5; proof of Lemma 8.4, p. 23
items.note: Used for the torsion of the descent obstruction in Lemma 1.1 (/2) and for Lemma 8.4 (/84). Review note: Should be planned, not missing. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#layer-2-isogenies-duality-and-the-weil-pairing (block 2B, 'Isogenies and quotients', step 1) plans 'the norm functor on invertible sheaves for finite locally free morphisms, including its base-change, tensor-product, and tower laws'. The identity Nm(π*L) ≅ L^{⊗n} should be requested there as part of that API. Remove /208 from route 1. Review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23): status changed from missing to planned; block 2B of that layer plans 'the norm functor on invertible sheaves for finite locally free morphisms, including its base-change, tensor-product, and tower laws', of which Nm(π*L) ≅ L^{⊗n} is part. Removed from its route.

items.name: Relatively minimal regular models and jacobian fibrations
items.statement: Let B be a regular curve over a field, or the spectrum of a DVR, with function field K, and C a regular proper curve over K with H⁰(C,O_C)=K and H¹(C,O_C) of dimension one. C has a unique relatively minimal regular proper model S→B. Its jacobian — the elliptic curve Pic⁰_{C/K}, or in the quasi-elliptic case the regular compactification of the twisted form Pic⁰_{C/K} of G_a — has a unique relatively minimal regular model with a section, the jacobian fibration J→B.
items.note: Lichtenbaum and Shafarevich for minimal models; /71, /75 and /81 use the output. Review note: Partly planned: tauceti StableReduction Layer 5 plans minimal regular models over a DVR for smooth projective generic fibres of positive genus. Missing are the regular but non-smooth (quasi-elliptic) generic fibre, the relatively minimal model over a curve B, and the jacobian fibration.

items.name: Enriques reducibility theorem (as used)
items.statement: (Lang 1983, Theorem 4.1) Let φ:Y→P¹ be a genus-one fibration of an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field. Every divisor class of degree two on the fibers contains, modulo vertical classes and multiples of a half-fiber, an integral curve R̃ with R̃²∈{0,−2}.
items.note: W. Lang, On Enriques surfaces in characteristic p. I, Math. Ann. 265 (1983), 45–65; stated as the paper uses it in /137 and /141. Review note: Lang 1983, Theorem 4.1 was not available, so the exact source statement is unverified. The form given follows from the usual Enriques reducibility lemma: decompose an integral two-section; exactly one summand has degree 1 on the half-fibre, and the rest is vertical. It holds over an algebraically closed field; the paper applies it over F₂, where the chosen curve must be descended by /67–/69.

items.name: Representability of the relative Picard functor (Artin)
items.statement: (Artin 1969, Theorem 7.3) For f:𝔜→Spec R flat, proper, of finite presentation and cohomologically flat in dimension zero, the fppf sheafification of A↦Pic(𝔜⊗_R A) is representable by a group algebraic space locally of finite presentation over R.
items.note: /49 and /50 specialize it to Enriques families with Ekedahl–Hyland–Shepherd-Barron, Corollary 4.3. Review note: Statement as the paper uses it. Artin's Theorem 7.3 is proved over bases of finite type over a field or an excellent Dedekind ring, and the arbitrary R of §5 follows by noetherian approximation, since Pic commutes with filtered limits. The node should say so.

items.name: Subgroups of the Picard functor and torsors under the Cartier dual (Raynaud)
items.statement: (Raynaud 1970, Proposition 6.2.1) Let f:𝔜→S be flat, proper and of finite presentation with f_*O=O, and P⊂Pic_{𝔜/S} a finite locally free commutative subgroup scheme with Cartier dual G=Hom(P,G_m). The inclusion corresponds to a global section of R¹f_*(G_𝔜); by the five-term sequence (2) it comes from a G-torsor over 𝔜 exactly when its image in H²(S,G) vanishes, and such torsors are unique up to pullbacks of G-torsors over S.
items.note: /55–/60 build the canonical coverings of Proposition 5.4 from it.

items.name: Picard scheme of a proper scheme over a field and its τ-part
items.statement: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k. The fppf sheaf Pic_{X/k} is represented by a commutative group scheme locally of finite type over k. The subfunctor Pic^τ_{X/k} parametrizes classes numerically trivial on the geometric fibre, i.e. of degree 0 on every integral curve in X_{k^alg}. It is an open and closed subgroup scheme of finite type. Hence Num_{X/k} = Pic_{X/k}/Pic^τ_{X/k} is an étale group scheme, and Num_{X/k}(k^alg) = Num_{X/k}(k^sep) is a free abelian group of finite rank ρ ≥ 0.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): /1 defines Num_{X/k} but no item states the existence and finiteness theorem behind it. Lemma 1.1, Theorem 1.3 and Proposition 5.3 all use it. Suggested owner: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1); /211 gives only algebraic-space representability in flat families, and no stage plans the τ-part or finite generation of Néron–Severi Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Pic^τ-torsor classes are killed by the splitting degree
items.statement: Let X be proper over a field k, P = Pic^τ_{X/k}, and l ∈ Num_{X/k}(k). The fibre T ⊂ Pic_{X/k} over l is a P-torsor. If T has a point over a finite extension E/k of degree n, then n·[T] = 0 in H¹_fppf(k, P), so n·l lifts to a k-point of Pic_{X/k}. The proof applies the norm N: R_{E/k}Pic^τ_{X_E/E} → Pic^τ_{X/k} with N∘pr* = n (/208), and uses that H¹(k, R_{E/k}P_E) → H¹(E, P_E) is injective by the five-term exact sequence.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the first half of the necessity proof of Lemma 1.1. It combines /208 with the five-term sequence, and no item states it. Suggested owner: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1) Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Brauer obstruction to representing Picard points
items.statement: Let h: X → S = Spec k be proper. The Leray spectral sequence for h and G_m gives an exact sequence Pic(X) → Pic_{X/k}(k) → H²(S, h_*G_{m,X}), whose first map is the canonical one. With /8, some positive multiple of every k-point of Pic_{X/k} is the class of an invertible sheaf on X.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the second half of Lemma 1.1 ('some multiple of l′ comes from an invertible sheaf'), also used in the Galois step of Theorem 1.3. /8 supplies only the torsion of the obstruction group. Suggested owner: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1); tauceti JacobianChallenge Layer D records the Br-flavoured obstruction only for curves with a section Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Semiample invertible sheaves and projective contractions
items.statement: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k and L a semiample invertible sheaf. Then R(X,L) = ⊕_{t≥0} H⁰(X, L^{⊗t}) is a finitely generated k-algebra, P(X,L) = Proj R(X,L) is projective, and the canonical morphism X → P(X,L) is a contraction. Every contraction f: X → Z with Z projective arises this way, from L = f*O_Z(1). R(X,L) and P(X,L) commute with field extension. Two numerically equivalent semiample invertible sheaves define isomorphic contractions, since each contracts exactly the integral curves on which it has degree zero.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The proof of Theorem 1.3 rests on the dictionary between semiample sheaves and projective contractions. It also silently uses that replacing L′ by ⊗_σ σ*L′ does not change the contraction. Suggested owner: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1) Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Descent of a contraction to a finite extension
items.statement: Let X be a proper k-scheme and f̄: X_{k^alg} → Ȳ a contraction with Ȳ projective. There are a finite subextension k ⊂ k′ ⊂ k^alg and a contraction f′: X_{k′} → Y′, with Y′ projective over k′, whose base change to k^alg is isomorphic to f̄.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): This spreading-out step descends the contraction from k^alg to a finite extension. No stage plans it for contractions of arbitrary proper schemes; tauceti ModularCurves 0E spreads out only relative curves. Suggested owner: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1), importing limit and descent machinery from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1 Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Descent along field extensions: global sections, properness, universal homeomorphism
items.statement: Let k ⊂ k′ be a field extension. (a) For a quasi-compact quasi-separated k-scheme U, Γ(U_{k′}, O) = Γ(U, O) ⊗_k k′. (b) A k-scheme Y is of finite type, separated, resp. proper over k if Y_{k′} is so over k′. (c) If k′/k is purely inseparable, X_{k′} → X is a universal homeomorphism for every k-scheme X.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The purely inseparable branch (/7) uses flat base change of global sections, descent of properness along k ⊂ k′, and that X_{k′} → X is a homeomorphism. Suggested owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1 (descent), which does not yet list descent of properness; otherwise NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1) Route: SchemeAndStackFoundations.

items.name: Brauer group of a finite algebra over a field
items.statement: Let R be a finite k-algebra and h: Spec R → S = Spec k. Then R^ih_*G_m = 0 for i = 1, 2: Pic of a semilocal ring is trivial, and H²(·, G_m) vanishes on finite products of strictly henselian local rings. So H²(S, h_*G_m) ≅ H²(Spec R, G_m) = Br(R). Moreover H²(Spec R, G_m) → H²(Spec R_red, G_m) is bijective, and R_red = ∏ K_i is a product of fields, so Br(R) ≅ ⊕_i Br(K_i) is torsion.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 1.4 (/8) reduces to the Brauer group of a finite k-algebra. The key input, that Brauer groups of fields are torsion, is stated by no item, and the étale Brauer group of a scheme is not planned (see /204's note). Suggested owner: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1), importing SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (étale cohomology of schemes); Pic of a semilocal ring is Mathlib (Mathlib/RingTheory/PicardGroup.lean:545) Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Contractions of smooth proper surfaces
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k with h⁰(O_S) = 1 and f: S → Z a contraction. Exactly one of the following holds: (a) Z = Spec k and f is the structure morphism; (b) Z is a geometrically normal proper surface and f is birational; (c) Z is a smooth proper geometrically connected curve, and f is flat with geometrically connected fibres (f is of fibre type).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The proof of Theorem 2.1 splits on this dichotomy, and no item states it. The printed version omits Z = Spec k (new issue). Suggested owner: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1) Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Negativity of exceptional curves (Mumford, Grauert)
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over a field and f: S → Z a proper birational morphism onto a normal surface. The irreducible components C_1, …, C_r of every one-dimensional fibre of f have negative-definite intersection matrix (C_i·C_j). Theorem 2.1 applies this after base change to Ω, which keeps Z normal.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the birational case of Theorem 2.1. /166 (Hodge index) does not state it. Suggested owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 (intersection theory on surfaces; it plans Hodge index but not this lemma), else NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1) Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Zariski's lemma for curves of fibre type
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over a field and C = Σ_{i=0}^r m_iC_i a connected curve of fibre type ((C·C_i) = 0 for all i). The intersection form on L = ⊕_i ZC_i is negative semidefinite, with radical Z·C_ind, where C_ind = C/gcd(m_i). Every proper subset of {C_0, …, C_r} spans a negative-definite sublattice; in particular C_i² < 0 for every i when r ≥ 1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The fibre-type case of Theorem 2.1 and the §3 terminology rely on it for arbitrary contractions onto curves over any field. /189 states it only for relatively minimal genus-one fibrations over algebraically closed fields. Suggested owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5, else NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1); route 2 imports it for /13 and /189 Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Zariski connectedness for contractions
items.statement: Let f: X → Z be a proper morphism of locally noetherian schemes with O_Z = f_*O_X. Then f is surjective, and every fibre f⁻¹(z) is geometrically connected over κ(z) (EGA III 4.3.1, 4.3.4).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The proof of Theorem 2.1 uses connectedness of geometric and schematic fibres twice. §3 also uses it ('the geometric fibre S_ā is a connected curve'). Suggested owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4 (formal functions), else NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent (route 1) Route: NumericalPicardAndContractionDescent.

items.name: Genus-one fibrations: elliptic, quasi-elliptic, relatively minimal
items.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k with h⁰(O_S) = 1. A genus-one fibration is a contraction f: S → B onto a smooth proper curve whose generic fibre S_η, a regular proper curve over k(B) with H⁰(O) = k(B), has h¹(O_{S_η}) = 1. It is elliptic if S_η is smooth over k(B), and quasi-elliptic otherwise; then char k ∈ {2, 3} and the geometric generic fibre is a rational cuspidal curve. It is relatively minimal if no fibre contains a (−1)-curve, equivalently (K_S·C) = 0 for every curve C in a fibre. Then every geometric fibre f⁻¹(ā) is a connected curve of canonical type.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): No item defines genus-one, elliptic, quasi-elliptic or relatively minimal fibrations. /169, /189, /190 and every later section use them. Suggested owner: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces (route 2) (Two checkers proposed this; merged with 'Genus-one fibration; elliptic and quasielliptic'.) Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Conductor squares for fibres with at most two components
items.statement: Let C be a proper curve of canonical type over a field F whose irreducible components are birational to P¹_F. (r = 1) If C is integral with h⁰(O_C) = h¹(O_C) = 1, its normalization P¹_F → C fits into a cartesian and cocartesian square with a closed subscheme Spec R ⊂ P¹_F of length two, contracted to a rational point Spec F ⊂ C. R ≅ F × F gives I₁; R ≅ F[ε]/(ε²) gives II; R a separable (resp. purely inseparable) quadratic field gives Ĩ₁ (resp. ĨI). (r = 2) If C = C_1 + C_2 with C_i ≅ P¹_F, then P¹ ⊔ P¹ → C fits into a cartesian and cocartesian square over Spec(R × R) → Spec R with R of length two, giving I₂, III, Ĩ₂, ĨII correspondingly. Over a perfect field ĨI and ĨII do not occur.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): /170–/171 cover only Ĩ₁ and Ĩ₂ over perfect fields. The general conductor-square description, which also gives I₁, II, ĨI, I₂, III, ĨII, underlies the counts of Proposition 3.2 and the r = 1 case of Proposition 9.2. Suggested owner: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces (route 2); generalizes /170–/171 Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Ordinary and supersingular elliptic curves
items.statement: An elliptic curve E over a field k of characteristic p > 0 is supersingular if E(k^alg) has no point of order p (equivalently, its Hasse invariant vanishes), and ordinary otherwise. In characteristic 2, with Weierstraß equation y² + a₁xy + a₃y = x³ + a₂x² + a₄x + a₆, E is supersingular iff a₁ = 0 iff j(E) = 0.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 3.3 (/20–/24), §4 (Lemma 4.3) and §§9–10 ('semistable or supersingular') use this definition, and no item gives it. Suggested owner: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces (route 2); the j-criterion rests on mathlib:WeierstrassCurve.j_eq_zero_iff_of_char_two (Weierstrass.lean:420) Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Normalization of curves under separable base change
items.statement: Let C be a reduced proper curve over a field k whose normalization C′ is smooth over k (automatic if k is perfect), and let k ⊂ Ω be a field extension. Then C_Ω is reduced and C′_Ω → C_Ω is its normalization.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The step (ii)⇒(iii) of /14 needs it, and it fails over imperfect fields without a smoothness hypothesis. Suggested owner: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces (route 2) or SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3 (curves) Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Curves of canonical type on an Enriques surface induce genus-one fibrations
items.statement: Let Y be an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field and C⊂Y an indecomposable curve of canonical type (/13). Then there is a unique genus-one fibration φ:Y→P¹ such that C is a fibre of φ or a half-fibre of φ, that is C or 2C is a fibre.
items.locator: §4, p. 12, sentence before Proposition 4.1 (Bombieri–Mumford 1977; Cossec–Dolgachev 1989, Chapter III); §4, p. 12; used in the proofs of Propositions 11.2–14.1, pp. 34–49
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): Used throughout §§11–14 to produce fibrations from configurations of (−2)-curves ('a curve of canonical type I₈ … contradiction', 'supports a curve of canonical type I₄*'), and underlies Proposition 4.1. No item covers it; /13 only defines curves of canonical type. Suggested owner: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence (new route) (Two checkers proposed this; merged with 'Curves of canonical type on Enriques surfaces'.) Route: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence.

items.name: (−2)-curve and two-section on an Enriques surface
items.statement: On an Enriques surface Y over an algebraically closed field, a (−2)-curve is an integral curve E with E²=−2; by adjunction (K_Y≡0) it is a smooth rational curve. Over an arbitrary field k, a (−2)-curve on Y is an integral curve E⊂Y whose base change to k̄ is a (−2)-curve. A two-section of a genus-one fibration φ is an integral curve C with C·φ^{-1}(∞)=2, equivalently C·F=1 for a half-fibre F.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1, p. 12; Proposition 4.4(ii), p. 13; Theorem 5.6(iii), p. 17
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 5.6(iii) descends (−2)-curves over a non-closed field, so the notion over k must be fixed. No item defines it. Suggested owner: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence (new route) Route: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence.

items.name: Low-degree Leray sequence for G_m and the Brauer obstruction
items.statement: Let f:𝔜→S be a flat proper finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces with O_S→f_*O_𝔜 an isomorphism universally. Then 0→Pic(S)→Pic(𝔜)→Pic_{𝔜/S}(S)→H²(S,G_m)→H²(𝔜,G_m) is exact (étale or fppf cohomology, which agree for G_m). In particular, if H²(S,G_m)=0, every S-point of Pic_{𝔜/S} is represented by an invertible sheaf on 𝔜.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the step that turns a section of the Picard scheme into a line bundle when H²(S,G_m)=0. /56 and /212 treat only the finite coefficient group G, and /182 needs a section. Suggested owner: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension (source, with /182, /211, /212); Leray spectral sequence from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 Route: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry.

items.name: Cohomology and base change for Enriques families
items.statement: Let f:𝔜→S be a flat proper finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces with S noetherian, and ℱ an S-flat coherent sheaf on 𝔜 with H^i(𝔜_s,ℱ_s)=0 for all i≥1 and all s∈S. Then f_*ℱ is locally free, its formation commutes with arbitrary base change, and f*f_*ℱ→ℱ is an isomorphism when ℱ is invertible and every ℱ_s is trivial.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The construction of the canonical cover over Z[1/2] (used in Proposition 5.5 and its repair) depends on it. Suggested owner: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension (the algebraic-space case)

items.name: Splitting of Z/2-extensions of a constant lattice over Spec Z
items.statement: Let S be a connected scheme over which every finite étale Z/2-torsor is trivial (for instance S=Spec Z, by /181). Every extension 0→(Z/2)_S→E→(Z^n)_S→0 of commutative group schemes over S splits. Hence an Enriques family over Z with Pic^τ=(Z/2)_Z and constant Num has Pic_{𝔜/Z}≅(Z/2×Z^{10})_Z.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the last step of Proposition 5.5 (P=Z/2 branch). It is mentioned only in the note of /62. Suggested owner: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence (new route) Route: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence.

items.name: A degree-one line bundle on a genus-one curve gives a rational point
items.statement: Let F be an integral proper curve over a field k with h⁰(O_F)=h¹(O_F)=1, and N an invertible sheaf on F of degree 1. Then χ(N)=1, so N has a nonzero section, whose zero scheme is an effective Cartier divisor of degree 1, that is a k-rational point of F.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): This gives the rational point, and hence B≅P¹, in the irreducible half-fibre case. /194 covers only the rational-curve case. Suggested owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3 (Riemann–Roch on proper curves); the consequence is stated in the node for /68–/69

items.name: Geometrically rational surface
items.statement: A proper surface J over a field k is geometrically rational if it is geometrically integral and J⊗k^alg is birational to P²_{k^alg}. Then h⁰(O_J)=1. If J is smooth, then b₁=0 and ρ(J̄)=b₂(J̄), and Pic_{J/k} is étale with torsion-free geometric group Pic(J̄)=Num(J̄).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The standing notion of §§6–10: it is in the hypotheses of Propositions 6.1–6.2, Corollary 7.3, Theorems 9.1 and 9.4, and all of §10. No item defines it. Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Geometric Frobenius on Tate-twisted cohomology
items.statement: Let X be proper over F_q (q=p^ν), ℓ≠p, Φ=F_X^ν⊗id the geometric (relative) Frobenius of X̄, and f_{i,j}=Φ* on H^i(X̄,Q_ℓ(j)). Under H^i(X̄,Q_ℓ(j))=H^i(X̄,Q_ℓ)⊗Q_ℓ(j), f_{i,j}=f_{i,0}⊗q^{−j}. If Z⊂X is a closed subscheme of pure codimension j defined over F_q, its cycle class in H^{2j}(X̄,Q_ℓ(j)) is fixed by f_{2j,j}.
items.locator: §7, p. 20 and proof of Proposition 7.1, p. 21
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The key step of Proposition 7.1: with cycles defined over F_q, f_{2j,j} is the identity. /201 records H^i(Q_ℓ(j))=H^i⊗Q_ℓ(j) but not the Frobenius action on the twist. Route: WeilConjectures.

items.name: Fibre counts of the jacobian match the Enriques surface
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be an Enriques surface with constant Picard scheme, φ:Y→P¹ an elliptic fibration, and J→P¹ its jacobian. For each a∈P¹(F₂), n_a (as defined in §9 from J_a) equals #Y_a(F₂). Hence Σ_{a∈P¹(F₂)} n_a=#Y(F₂)=25.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): This is how Theorem 9.1 follows from Theorem 9.4: the hypothesis Σn_a=25 is checked on the Enriques surface. It uses Proposition 9.2 for simple fibres and Corollary 8.3 for multiple fibres with smooth reduction. No item states it; /95 only defines n_a. Route: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence.

items.name: Generation of Picard groups of genus-one fibrations (Shioda–Tate)
items.statement: (a) Let f:S→B be a genus-one fibration of a smooth proper surface over a field, with generic fibre S_F, and R⊂S a horizontal divisor of degree d>0 on S_F such that d divides the degree on S_F of every line bundle on S. The kernel of Pic(S)→Pic⁰(S_F), L↦(L−(deg(L|S_F)/d)R)|S_F, is generated by the irreducible components of the closed fibres and by R, and the map is surjective. (b) If f has a section O, then Pic(S) is generated by O, a fibre, the vertical curves disjoint from O and the sections, and MW(S/B)=Pic⁰(S_F)=S_F(F).
items.locator: proof of Proposition 9.3(v), p. 25; after Theorem 9.4, p. 26
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): Two Shioda–Tate-type generation statements, used in Proposition 9.3(v) and in reducing Theorem 9.4 to Proposition 9.5. /98 only covers the complement W for a rational jacobian. Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 12 (I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂)
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of y²+txy+t³y=x³+x² has Δ=t¹⁰, j=t², fibres I₂* at t=0 (all components rational), E₄ at t=1, non-split I₂ at ∞, and no other singular fibre. It has constant Picard scheme (#J(F₂)=15+4+6=25) and satisfies condition (ii) of §10.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): A model missing from the printed Theorem 10.4 but required by the corrected classification (/115). Proposition 11.1 must treat it. Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 13 (I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁)
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of y²+txy+t³y=x³+tx² has Δ=t¹¹, j=t, fibres I₃* at t=0 (all components rational), E₄ at t=1, non-split I₁ at ∞, and no other singular fibre. It has constant Picard scheme (#J(F₂)=17+4+4=25) and satisfies condition (ii).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): As above. Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Rational elliptic model 14 (IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂)
items.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of y²+txy+t²y=x³+t²x² has Δ=t⁸(t²+t+1), j=t⁴/(t²+t+1). Its fibres are IV* at t=0 (all components rational), E₄ at t=1, non-split I₂ at ∞, and I₁ over the point t²+t+1=0. It has constant Picard scheme (#J(F₂)=15+4+6=25) and satisfies condition (ii).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): As above. Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

items.name: Point-count criterion for constant Picard scheme of a rational surface
items.statement: Let J be a smooth projective geometrically rational surface over F_q with ρ=b₂(J̄)=r. Then Pic_{J/F_q} is constant if and only if #J(F_q)=1+rq+q². Proof: H²(J̄,Q_ℓ(1))=NS(J̄)⊗Q_ℓ, so #J(F_q)=1+q·Tr(σ|NS(J̄))+q². σ has finite order, so trace r forces σ=id.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): Condition (i) of §10 (constant Pic) is not directly computable from a Weierstrass equation. This criterion makes it computable. With Tate's algorithm it turns Theorems 10.4 and 10.5 into a finite check over the 2²¹ equations, without Lang 2000 (/198). That check is how the missing models were found. Route: WeilConjectures.

items.name: Every half-fibre has a partner (Cossec–Dolgachev)
items.statement: Let Y be an Enriques surface over an algebraically closed field. If Y is not extra-special of type Ẽ₈, then for every half-fibre F there is a half-fibre F′ of another genus-one fibration with F·F′=1 (every 1-sequence extends to a 2-sequence). Extra-special surfaces exist only in characteristic 2. An extra-special surface of type Ẽ₈ has exactly one genus-one fibration.
items.locator: Cossec–Dolgachev 1989, Theorem 3.4.1 (as quoted in arXiv:2201.05481, Theorem 1.2 and Remark 1.5); main paper proof of Proposition 4.4(iii), p. 13
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): /45 states the partner fibration only for nonexceptional surfaces in characteristic 2, as Proposition 4.4 does. But Proposition 11.2 (no nonexceptional hypothesis) and Proposition 14.1 (arbitrary p) need it more generally; see the new sourceIssues. The general form is quoted by Martin–Mezzedimi–Veniani, arXiv:2201.05481, Theorem 1.2 ('[CD, Theorem 3.4.1] or [CDL, Theorem 6.1.10]') and Remark 1.5. Suggested owner: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence; /45 becomes its corollary once 'nonexceptional ⇒ not extra-special of type Ẽ₈' is checked in Ekedahl–Shepherd-Barron / CDL (not verified here) Route: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence.

items.name: Incidences of the generating two-section
items.statement: Let Y/F₂ be a nonexceptional Enriques surface with constant Picard scheme, and φ a genus-one fibration with simple fibre φ⁻¹(∞)=C₀+C₁+2(C₂+⋯+C₆)+C₇+C₈ (C₀,C₁ meeting C₂; C₇,C₈ meeting C₆). Let S⊂Num(Y) be either ⟨C₁,…,C₈,R,F⟩ for a (−2)-curve R meeting only C₄ (Proposition 12.2), or ⟨C₁,…,C₈,F′,F⟩ with F′ the half-fibre of the second I₄* fibration (Proposition 12.3). Let R̃ be an integral two-section of φ with Num(Y)=S+ZR̃. Then R̃≡C₇* or C₈* mod S, and (R̃·C₀,…,R̃·C₈) has exactly two entries equal to 1 and the rest 0, the pair being {C₀,C₈} or {C₁,C₇} (class C₈*) or {C₀,C₇} or {C₁,C₈} (class C₇*). In the first setting the symmetries C₀↔C₁, C₇↔C₈ preserve S, so one may assume R̃·C₀=R̃·C₈=1. In the second setting only C₇↔C₈ is available, leaving {C₀,C₈} and {C₁,C₈}.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 12.2, p. 42; proof of Proposition 12.3, pp. 43–44
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The extraction itemizes the incidence case lists of Propositions 12.1 (/134) and 13.2 (/144), but not the lattice-theoretic case list for R̃, which is where the paper's reasoning is faulty (new sourceIssue). Recomputed with N⁻¹ from (14) and (16) (S/rv4_lattice.py). Suggested owner: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence; imports /136, /140, /155, /157 Route: EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence.

items.name: Riemann–Roch on a genus-one curve
items.statement: Let C be a regular proper geometrically integral curve of arithmetic genus 1 over a field K. For every line bundle L on C with deg L≥1, h⁰(L)=deg L. In particular every degree-2 line bundle is O_C(D) for an effective divisor D of degree 2, and if C has no divisor of degree 1, then D is a single closed point of degree 2.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 12.2, p. 42; proof of Theorem 5.6, p. 17
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The Riemann–Roch used here is on the generic genus-one curve Y_K over K=F₂(t), not surface Riemann–Roch (/164, whose locator wrongly includes §12). It produces the integral two-section R̃ on which Propositions 12.2 and 12.3 rest. Suggested owner: Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves Layer 5 ('deg D≥2g−1 ⟹ ℓ(D)=deg D+1−g') with the Layer 12 function-field/curve dictionary

items.name: Picard group of the generic fibre of a fibred surface
items.statement: Let f:S→B be a proper flat morphism from a regular integral noetherian surface to a regular integral one-dimensional base with f_*O_S=O_B, and K the function field of B. Then restriction Pic(S)→Pic(S_K) is surjective, and its kernel is generated by f*Pic(B) and the classes O_S(C) of the irreducible components C of closed fibres. If S=Y is an Enriques surface over a field and f is a genus-one fibration with an integral two-section R, then L↦(L−(L·F)R)|_{Y_K} (F a half-fibre) factors through Num(Y) and induces Num(Y)/T≅Pic⁰(Y_K), where T is generated by R, F and the vertical (−2)-curves.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 9.3(v), p. 25; proofs of Propositions 12.2 and 12.3, pp. 42–43
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (coverage of the paper): The identifications Pic⁰(Y_K)=Num(Y)/S (/137, /141) and MW(J/P¹)=Pic⁰(Y_F) (/94) rest on this general fact, which no item states. Suggested owner: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces (part-ii route) for the first sentence; EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence for the Enriques identification Route: GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces.

source.title: There is no Enriques surface over the integers
source.versionRead: Author's third revised version,19 July 2022,52 pages; compared with arXiv v3,9 August 2022. The body after the first page has identical extracted text; first-page differences are watermark/indentation. Publisher revision date agrees. The 63-page typeset publication was not obtained, so corrections below apply to the public preprint, not automatically the published version.
readSections: Schröer 2021: Theorem 2.5; Corollaries 5.4–5.5, Theorem 6.1 and proof; §7 through Theorem 7.2 proof
Fontaine 1993: scanned author introduction, Theorem 1 and remark(a), PDF pages 2–4
Liu–Lorenzini–Raynaud 2004: Corollary 6.5, Theorem 6.6 and proof, Remark 6.8, pp. 495–497
Liu–Lorenzini–Raynaud 2018 corrigendum: introduction and corrected statements, pp. 593–595
arXiv v3 TeX source, read in full (continuation cc-442dc5)

Review REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026): arXiv v3 (the same PDF, SHA-256 ae6481f2…) and its TeX source read in full again with four checkers, every item checked against it; the matrices (14) and (16) and the eleven printed Weierstrass models recomputed, and all 2²¹ Weierstrass equations over F₂ classified by Tate's algorithm. The published version is paywalled and was not available to the review either.

continuations.readExtent: Full 52-page author paper reread. All diagrams on pages 34–38,40–44,46–48 inspected; table/matrix pages 14, 29, 33, 41, 43 inspected. Fontaine PDF pages 2–4 reread visually. Conrad Theorems 3.2, 4.1, 4.5 and the proof of 4.5 read; not the full 25-page note. Stacks 0H74,0EMV Lemma 68.11.4,0D24 Lemma 99.11.4,0D3A,0D3D read with proofs. Earlier prerequisite reading records belong to codex-a71f92 and are preserved, not claimed as repeated.

The arXiv v3 TeX source (EnriquesOverIntegers.tex, 228,086 bytes; e-print SHA-256 ae77260256b42df57443f3101ccda9bf2bbbc2f991410bf27f02b0e0afdc87d9) was read in full, with the arXiv v3 PDF. Statement and equation numbers were simulated from the TeX counters (excluding \iffalse blocks) and matched to every numbered heading of the PDF. Independently recomputed: the eleven Weierstrass equations of Theorems 10.4–10.5 (discriminant orders at t = 0, 1, ∞, j-invariants, and point counts of the smooth fibers at t = 1 and t = ∞), and the Gram matrices (14) and (16) with determinant −4. The repairs of Propositions 5.5, 9.3(v) and 9.5 in /63, /94 and /97 were checked independently. The cited prerequisites (Lang 2000, Lang 1983, Cossec–Dolgachev, Ekedahl–Shepherd-Barron, Liu–Lorenzini–Raynaud, Fontaine 1993) were not re-read; their statements enter as the items /189–/212 and the earlier items that cite them.

summary: Schröer proves that there is no smooth proper family of Enriques surfaces over ℤ (Theorem 5.1). Over ℤ the Picard scheme of such a family would be constant (Proposition 5.5, using Minkowski, Br(ℤ) = 0 and Fontaine's bound on the Hodge numbers of varieties with good reduction everywhere); its fiber over F₂ would be non-exceptional (it lifts to ℤ/4ℤ); and no non-exceptional Enriques surface over F₂ has constant Picard scheme (Theorem 15.1). That last theorem rests on descent of curves and fibrations from F̄₂ (Theorem 5.6), a count of 25 rational points (Corollary 7.3), the transfer of constant Picard scheme to rational jacobian surfaces (Theorem 9.1), the classification of eleven Weierstrass equations over F₂[t] (Theorems 10.4–10.5), and a combinatorial elimination of fiber configurations (§§11–14) that uses Nikulin's discriminant forms. The atlas has no Enriques or elliptic surfaces, no genus-one fibrations and no Picard schemes of proper schemes over a field; it plans Tate's algorithm, surface intersection theory, the Weil conjectures and cycle classes, and Tau Ceti has the discriminant-form and overlattice library. 212 items (16 library, 12 planned, 184 missing) are routed to nine routes: a new roadmap for Enriques surfaces and the nonexistence proof, Part IIs of NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties (genus-one fibrations and rational elliptic surfaces), AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry (numerical Picard groups and contraction descent) and SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCases (low-degree Hodge obstructions), and sources for R07.1, WC.7, IG.0, A0-extension and SF.1–SF.2. Seventeen mistakes are recorded, including a gap in the proof of Proposition 5.5 (the canonical covers over ℤ[1/2] and over W(F̄₂) are compared without their twists) and the false claim Br(F₂(t)) = 0 in Proposition 9.3; both are repaired. After the review (REV-PAPER-SCHROER-23) there are 245 items (16 library, 15 planned, 214 missing) and 44 source issues. The most serious is that Theorem 10.4's list of rational elliptic surfaces is incomplete (three further models, found by exhaustive search), which leaves a gap in the proof of Theorem 15.1 and hence of the main theorem. The extraction's own repair of the Proposition 5.5 gap is sound.

routes.title: Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry, Part II: numerical Picard groups and contraction descent

routes.brief: Start from Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry), especially A0-extension, and Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1,SF.2,SF.5). Construct Pic^τ and Num for arbitrary proper schemes over a field, including nonreduced and disconnected schemes; expose geometric base change, Galois action, numerical equivalence, torsion obstructions and norm maps. Prove the positive-power descent criterion with a numerically trivial twist, then Theorem 1.3: constant Num descends geometric contractions with projective target; treat purely inseparable descent separately without the constantness assumption. Prove Theorem 2.1 for contractions of smooth proper surfaces: component-graph descent, the geometrically-reduced edge-label assertion, and pure inseparability of residue fields of reducible fibers. Import surface intersections, not their reconstruction. Give each definition an API and at least three tests; include P¹_C/R with permuted numerical components, d=0 as a forbidden criterion, and projectivity versus arbitrary proper targets. The Enriques roadmap consumes these general theorems; it must not own a duplicate Picard theory. Add the killed-by-two numerical-class lift /183 as a sheaf-quotient construction. Import rigidified Picard descent from A0-extension and relative ampleness from R09.1/R09.3; the Enriques consumer owns the local-projectivity application.

routes.brief: Build on Néron models and semistable abelian varieties (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.2,R11.4), Elliptic curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves, Layer 4), and Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3–SF.5). Cover regular minimal genus-one models, elliptic versus quasielliptic generic fibers, fiber multiplicities versus reduced and indecomposable divisors, geometric Kodaira types and finite-field nonsplit I₁/I₂ forms. Import the Tate algorithm, not a second algorithm. Prove the excellent-DVR isogeny theorem 8.1, extension-count corollary and special F₂ isomorphism; use Liu–Lorenzini–Raynaud 6.6 only with algebraically closed residue field. Construct the degree-bounded two-chart Weierstrass model of a smooth rational Jacobian. End with Theorem 9.4's precisely conditioned Picard-constancy criterion and Theorems 10.4/10.5: eleven nonzero-j and three zero-j models under constant Picard and at most one rational semistable/supersingular fiber. The paper's Theorem 10.4 lists eight nonzero-j models. The review found three more with an exhaustive search over F₂, checked by Tate's algorithm and point counts: y²+txy+t³y=x³+x² (I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂), y²+txy+t³y=x³+tx² (I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁) and y²+txy+t²y=x³+t²x² (IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂). Plan the classification as that finite computation: for geometrically rational J, constant Picard is equivalent to #J(F₂) = 25. Acquire Lang 2000 and verify its classification, including coordinate equivalence and Kodaira resolutions, before asserting completeness. Import Tau Ceti's IntegralLattices implementation for discriminants; separately prove its geometric lattice realization. Test the five F₂ curves, all 11 equation invariants, the degree-two I₁ exception, and the distinction between split component graph and split nodes. Also cover the general inputs the proofs use, each as its own node: the Kodaira–Néron classification of fibers (/189) and Szydło's schematic fibers over non-closed fields (/190); the canonical bundle formula (/191) and tame versus wild multiple fibers (/192); relatively minimal regular models and jacobian fibrations, elliptic and quasi-elliptic (/209); the invariants of rational elliptic surfaces (/196) and quasi-elliptic fibrations in characteristic 2 (/197); Lang's theorem on torsors over finite fields (/193), twisted forms of P¹ (/194), isogeny invariance of point counts (/195) and Tsen's theorem over algebraically closed constants (/206); and Lang's 2000 classification in the form the paper uses it (/198), from the source itself.

sourceIssues.correction: Also treat the case where C′₁+C′₂ lies in ψ⁻¹(∞), the simple fibre already containing C₁+⋯+C₅.
